## Reporting clock: exact source and distinction from finding 297

The preserved neutral packet quotes district finding 297 in full: the marital-rape exception does not extend to coercive sexual behavior other than penetration; the 90-day reporting requirement in §3128(c) further narrows the class because many women may be unable to discuss or report rape for years after the incident. The finding does **not** itself quote the full subsection or expressly repeat its clock-start words. Do not put statutory words inside a quotation attributed to finding 297.

The contemporaneous enacted statute independently supplies those words. Act of December 21, 1984, P.L. 1210, No. 230, §2, at P.L. 1211, added §3128(c):

> (c) Crime to be reported.—The crime of spousal sexual assault shall be personally reported by the victim or her agent to a law enforcement agency having the requisite jurisdiction within 90 days of the commission of the offense.

Official source: [Pennsylvania Legislative Reference Bureau, 1984 Act 230, p. 1211](https://www.palrb.gov/getfile.cfm?file=resources%2Fpreservation-project%2Fpltiftopdf%2F19001999%2F1984%2F0%2Fact%2F0230.pdf&view=true). Full 12-page PDF, P.L.1210–1221, downloaded through Node after Windows TLS retrieval failed; all extracted pages were read in this verification (`1984-act-230.pdf`, `1984-act-230.txt`). No PDF skim or inference from its first pages. PDF visual renderer unavailable at the expected Poppler path; the operative text is independently corroborated in official enrolled bill HB281 PN3731 and the existing district source. The statute is a pre-cutoff source; the 1992 proposed repeal material found during discovery was not used as governing law.

Recommended source-qualified sentence: “The reported-spousal-assault exception incorporates §3128(c)'s requirement that the victim or her agent personally report the offense to a law-enforcement agency with jurisdiction within 90 days **of the commission of the offense**. District finding 297 describes how that limit excludes women unable to report for years after the incident.” This is not a period beginning at discovery of pregnancy, a request for abortion, notification, or discovery that the conduct was unlawful.

## Statutory completeness capsule

All quoted statute text in the baseline is preserved from the user's source. The following distinctions were reverified against it:

- §3203: physician's good-faith clinical judgment; immediate abortion to avert death, or delay creating serious risk of substantial and irreversible impairment of a major bodily function. The Third Circuit's prospective significant-threat construction is judicial construction, not added statutory wording.
- §3205(b): explain the emergency medical indications **before abortion if possible**. It does not require an explanation to delay necessary treatment.
- §3205(c): physician's defense to failure to furnish subsection (a) information, proved by a preponderance, based on reasonable belief that furnishing information would severely adversely affect physical or mental health. This is separate from emergency treatment and no general waiting-period waiver. The source's `(e) Penalty` label is a known OCR error; both lower courts identify `(c)`. The supplied source remains untouched. Likewise the source's §3208 `(e) Free distribution` is the `(c)` identified in district finding 177; no change in substance.
- §3205(a)(1): oral medical information by performing or referring physician; procedure, material risks/alternatives, probable gestational age, childbirth medical risks; 24-hour timing is a separable duty, subject to medical emergency.
- §3205(a)(2): performing/referring physician or expressly delegated qualified physician assistant, health-care practitioner, technician, or social worker may give ancillary notices. Materials are free and optional; medical assistance **may** be available. Paternal support liability continues despite the father's offer to pay for abortion. **“In the case of rape, this information may be omitted.”** It is permission, not mandatory omission; no police-reporting condition; no elimination of the support obligation; no merger with §3209(b)(3).
- §3205(a)(3)–(4): supply materials if chosen; no required acceptance, reading, or endorsement. Written certification records provision of required information, not ideological assent.
- §3206: unemancipated under-18 minor and distinct adult-incompetence text; only the minor challenge is developed. One-parent informed consent ordinarily; mother alone for paternal incest; guardian for deceased/unavailable parents within reasonable time/manner; custodial parent after divorce; adult standing in place of parent when parent/guardian unavailable. Parent/guardian considers only best interests. Emergency excuses. Minor may choose court without asking parent first. Mature/capable plus actually informed consent **or** best interests supplies authorization. Counsel absent private counsel or knowing intelligent waiver; confidentiality; trial ruling within three business days, appeal within five business days. Three-plus-five business days describes judicial ruling periods, not an invented eight-calendar-day statutory clock. Statute has no express parental clinic-visit command; district practice finding and appellate footnote 23 reservation remain distinct.
- §3209: signed nonnotarized notice certificate warning of punishable falsity; signed nonnotarized exception certificate with the same warning establishes at least one of nonpaternity, unsuccessful diligent location effort, pregnancy from reported §3128 spousal sexual assault, or reason to believe notice likely causes bodily injury to woman by spouse or another individual. Medical emergency separately excuses. No generic exception for psychological/economic coercion, injury to others, publicity, divorce, or custody consequences. §3128(a)–(b) elements are sexual/deviate intercourse by forcible compulsion, qualifying threat, or with unconscious spouse. Penalty is unprofessional conduct with license suspension/revocation through governing procedures; knowing violations additionally create spouse-father's civil damages, $5,000 punitive damages, and prevailing-plaintiff reasonable attorney fee.
- §3214(a): individual procedure report excludes patient name; confidentiality adequacy was accepted. Referring physician, agency, or service in (a)(1) is separate from performing/concurring/second-physician/facility identification. (a)(8) documents necessity under §3211(b)(1); (a)(10) emergency basis; (a)(11) actual prudent gestational-age inquiries/exams/tests/basis under §3210(a), whose emergency-prevents-compliance exception remains. (a)(5) is age result, a different field. (a)(12) separates marital status from notice and reasons for no notice.
- §3207(b) public facility/affiliation reports: State funds within 12 calendar months before inspection/copying **request**. Nonfunded reports available only to law-enforcement officials and medical boards for official duties. §3214(f) quarterly/trimester totals: State funds within 12 calendar months before **filing**; no-funding statement triggers confidential treatment absent contrary evidence. Agency collection and public release are distinct; no invented public patient identity disclosure.
- Act 64 §6 and Pennsylvania general severability law permit words, phrases, provisions, and applications to remain operative where independently effective. No automatic all-or-nothing Act remedy follows.

## O'Connor and Kennedy refrozen pre-Stone boundaries

These are preserved pre-Stone conclusions, not assignments or post-Stone joins. Sources and full two-path rows are the version 1.2 annex's “provisional all eight” and “reconciled all eight,” especially the O'Connor/Kennedy matrices.

O'Connor: Akron and Thornburgh dissents first require severe access restriction/absolute obstacle, then compelling justification; she rejects a universal meaningful-burden evidentiary shift, universal least-restrictive-means demand below severity, and automatic invalidity of **every** severe obstacle. A independently categorical anti-veto boundary is permissible. She retains protected previability choice and effective life/health protection, rejects the rigid trimester machinery, allows truthful encouragement and reasonable regulation below severity, and requires actual rather than presumed burdens. Her independent Hogan equality and narrow adult-family privacy theories address spousal notice only. Stare decisis is component-specific, with ordinary workability/reliance reasoning, no special legitimacy rule arising merely from controversy.

Kennedy: Webster join, Hodgson writing, Ohio v. Akron, Michael H. concurrence join, and Payne concurrence join support retained choice, rejection of trimester machinery, reasonable nonpreclusive regulation, useful medical responsibility, and a particular ban on adult third-party control. He has **no** frozen universal strict-severe/obstacle formula; serious medical regulation remains source/context-specific. He refuses a universal meaningful-burden State proof shift and a label-driven new test. Protected choice and health safeguards can be stated independently; institutional controversy alone supplies no stare-decisis rule. Independent equality and general informational-privacy grounds remain unadopted; narrow decision autonomy supports notice invalidation.

Both preserve the verified record and statutory qualifications. Both sustain emergency construction, accurate content/ancillary notice/optional materials/certification, physician delivery, waiting, parental informed-consent/bypass including the assumed attendance operation, confidential referral and medical-basis reporting, and public facility disclosure on their own grounds; both invalidate spousal notice and notice/reason reports and retain separable marital status. Those frozen judgments are not presumed joins to any new Stone rationale or any opinion majority. Every version 1.3 proposition needs a fresh compatibility test.

## Framework commitments and barriers

| Proposition | Blackmun | Stevens | Souter |
|---|---|---|---|
| Protected previability choice, viability, necessary postviability life/health care | Joins protected liberty from own Roe/Webster; no medical-reasons approval for previability choice | Joins from Thornburgh/Webster/Hodgson | Retains precedent under Payne special-justification rule; no invented prior abortion philosophy |
| Substantial obstacle to protected safe care independently forbidden | Joins as floor; does not replace stricter staged scrutiny | Joins floor; refuses obstacle-only safe harbor | Joins floor; refuses treating every lesser burden as automatically valid |
| Lesser meaningful burden and State justification | Joins inadequate-fit invalidity as minimum, retains stricter important-health/compelling/tailoring rules | Supports meaningful-burden justification/fit and State burden under own Hodgson; no perfection or trivial-cost rule | Requires justification where existing abortion precedent does, can join concrete inadequate-fit applications; refuses universal new burden-shifting/balancing formula without separate justified reconciliation |
| Trimester timetable | Refuses general abolition; existing law already allows some first-trimester regulation, which is distinct from removing staged safeguards | Replacement conditional on operative meaningful justification/fit protections, not existence of congenial minority proposal | Applies entering precedents; refuses categorical abolition absent specific special justification and preserved protection; general replacement remains bounded question |
| Stare decisis | Retain Roe/Akron/Thornburgh actual protective rules, distinguish materially different true content/confidentiality; reproductive reliance | Retain foundation/viability; justified precise refinement permitted if protective grounds survive | Constitutional error alone insufficient; actual special justification needed, partial correction possible; direct delay/delegation precedents remain |
| Clinical evidence/enforcement | Join competent evidence and individualized judgment, no professional organizational veto, no immunity for malpractice/fraud | Same; actual clinical departures require reasons, no mandatory useless tests | Joins bounded existing clinical inquiry and prospective good-faith enforcement; does not thereby join universal transfer for every regulation |
| Broad severe-interference/strict-justification minimum | Frozen scrutiny is at least as protective; a floor is possible only with stronger protections reserved | Heightened protection and actual-fit method supply basis for minimum, but precise operative formulation still needs post-v1.3 test | **No exact general severe-interference/compelling-interest formulation was frozen.** Existing clinical-liberty and abortion precedents may support a bounded minimum; must test its scope separately and explain any generalization rather than infer from label, Riggins, or frozen obstacle prohibition |

The last row is not a new Souter refusal to any precisely formulated severe-interference minimum: that formulation has not yet been opened. It identifies the absence of a preauthorized comprehensive join and the need for an exact test. Blackmun likewise cannot be counted for the complete replacement merely because a minimum is compatible.

## Exact component dispositions

All three sustain prospective emergency protection (not harm already realized); ordinary accurate material medical disclosures, statutory publication/elective receipt, and receipt certification only for lawful duties; all invalidate adult physician-only delivery and the fixed 24-hour interval; all invalidate spousal notice and the notice-given/nonnotice-reason subfields, preserving confidential marital status; all sustain (a)(8), (10), (11) confidential medical-basis reports at their distinct predicates and safeguards.

Rape permission does not cure residual compelled unrelated counseling. | Sustain narrow truthful notices facially with exact qualifications; concrete misleading implementation open | Same limited facial sustention; no broad permission to compel any truthful fact |

Separately invalidate incorporated mandatory ancillary content only | Sustain accurate informed-parent content/core/bypass; no attendance vacatur/remand, retain actual enforced-visit challenge | Same result; no universal holding bypass cures every needless visit |

Souter fallback precision: lines 1716, 1720, 1726 and reconciliation lines 2117/2123/2166–2178 retain direct Akron grounds for adult delay and exclusive counseling without requiring a comprehensive new test. His report votes are **not** a fallback invalidation: (a)(1), public-release and three medical-basis reports are sustained for their particular legitimate functions, narrow scope and proof. Danforth confidentiality supports lawful reporting; it does not invalidate referrals or public release by itself. His ordinary medical information/emergency/parental applications can be joined at Roe/Doe/Danforth/minors-case scope without adopting Stone-specific doctrines.

## Expressly unresolved or declined grounds

All three decline an independently sufficient equal-protection, general marital-privacy, informational-privacy, or spousal First Amendment holding; private autonomy/coercion informs abortion-liberty reasoning only. Spousal speech and its preservation remain open because liberty relief is complete. Standalone emergency vagueness/preservation remains open; the facial health/construction judgment does not reject vagueness. No generalized numerical facial formula or universal large-fraction replacement is frozen; all accept evaluating actually burdened women and appropriate severed relief. No separate materials/attendance remand is required by their final frozen rows. No unappealed collection/ascertainment/new adult-incompetence question is reopened.

## Statute/record check

All essential unchanged premises survive: §3205(a)(2)(iii) permits rape omission, imposes no police condition, changes no liability; §3205(c) is separate preponderance reasonable-belief defense for severely adverse physical/mental health from disclosure, not a waiver of treatment delay; §3206 has no enacted clinic visit or automatic incorporation of every §3205 delivery mechanism; (a)(11) records actual prudent diagnostic steps/basis, distinct from age result; public-release lookbacks differ (request for §3207(b), filing for §3214(f)); no patient confidentiality leak is found. Prior finding297 quoted 90 days with incident context but did not itself print full §3128(c); parent independently verifies the official commission-of-offense clock without changed premise.

## Comparator status

All original BSS commitments survive historical reconciliation. Material interpretive departures already openly documented include Blackmun sustaining medical-basis reports/no attendance remand; Stevens sustaining actual ancillary/gestational content and invalidating referrer identities; Souter retaining direct Akron delay/exclusivity rules and declining a comprehensive replacement. No historical source correction moves a vote. User-authorized reuse preserves this reconciliation; v1.3 changes to Stone must not rewrite those pre-Stone conclusions by implication.

### New proposition-level compatibility and final-part tests

# Blackmun, Stevens and Souter - final proposition, judgment and assignment audit

Scope: all 31 public holdings, 34 judgment components, 49 opinion parts and 33 assignments, together with the published separate positions, standing-fallback disclosure and legal limits. Each formulation is tested against the refrozen Justice-specific commitments and supported narrower positions. No version 1.2 post-Stone joins, authorship, assignments or judgment aggregation enters this assembly. The research cutoff is June 29, 1992. The underlying run uses single-conversation mode; true blindness was unavailable.

## Determination

The final joins, refusals, judgments, explanations and assignments are compatible with the preserved BSS commitments and the express section 8 reconciliations. Blackmun joins the bounded independent speech grounds for voluntary materials and basic receipt certification; he leaves the independent speech grounds for the three mandatory ancillary notices undecided after invalidating those commands on due process grounds. Basic documentation, ancillary certification and timing/delivery certification retain distinct rationale and judgment coalitions. Souter joins the limited necessary severe-access floor through express resolution of his reserved formulation question and retains his provision-specific precedent grounds. Stevens joins the complete substantive proposal through the separately recorded supported refinement; that proposal remains noncontrolling and changes none of his component judgments.

Stone's standing fallback applies only to the named independent medical-content, ancillary-notice, chosen-materials and basic-certificate speech claims, and the separately presented incorporation of the three ancillary notices into parental informed consent. Section II does not expressly address those independently presented claims or components. His fallback adds the majority disposition and no ground. His judgment participation authorizes assignment where applicable; it does not create a rationale signature.

## Source keys and frozen boundaries

- **BR**: Blackmun's *Roe* majority, 410 U.S. 113, 152–165. Protected decision, staged scrutiny, viability and health protection.
- **BT**: Blackmun's *Thornburgh* majority, 476 U.S. 747, 759–771, with Stevens's actual join. Individual clinical judgment, compelled counseling and reporting examined by their real function and interference.
- **BW**: Blackmun's *Webster* separate opinion, 492 U.S. 490, 537–560. Retains stronger Roe protection; does not assent to a weaker exclusive replacement.
- **BA**: Blackmun's *Ashcroft* separate opinion, 462 U.S. 476, 494–505, with Stevens's actual join. Distinguishes useful records/safeguards from unsupported professional requirements; parental safeguards remain provision-specific.
- **BO**: Blackmun's *Ohio v. Akron* dissent, 497 U.S. 502, 525–542. Tests practical operation and actual safeguards.
- **ST**: Stevens's *Thornburgh* concurrence, 476 U.S. 747, 772–782. Protected childbearing decision and distinct interests rather than ordinary economic deference.
- **SW**: Stevens's *Webster* separate opinion, 492 U.S. 490, 560–572. Text, function, actual medical use and limits of facial adjudication.
- **SH**: Stevens's *Hodgson* writing, 497 U.S. 417, relevant Parts III and V–VIII with notes. Actual family operation, permissible purpose and fit, alternatives and meaningful interference.
- **SO**: Stevens's *Ohio v. Akron* concurrence, 497 U.S. 502, 521–525, and actual joins to Parts I–IV. No-valid-applications language at 514 is in II-A and was joined by Stevens; this audit does not relocate it to unjoined Part V.
- **SR**: Stevens's actual *Riley* joins, 487 U.S. 781. Compensation does not categorically remove speech protection.
- **SP**: Souter's *Payne* concurrence, 501 U.S. 808, 842–856. Special justification, precise precedent treatment, preserved safeguards; no invented pre-Casey abortion opinion.
- **Carey**: 431 U.S. 678, 686–690 and n.5; complete official CAP text including all opinions/notes read. Blackmun and Stevens actually joined Parts II and III. Exacting justification attaches to materially limited access to the protected decision, not every reproductive regulation. For Souter this is entering precedent applied through SP, not a fabricated prior personal abortion writing.
- **Akron / Doe / Danforth / minors**: entering provision-specific precedents retained or displaced at expressly stated scopes. Souter's SP method supplies his own reason to apply these authorities; their mere existence does not automatically allocate every other Justice's join.
- **Simulated corroboration**: actual bounded BSS commitments in *Foucha*, *Riggins*, *Quill*, *Hilton*, *Medina*, *Collins*, *Wright* and *Lee*, as recorded in the preserved pre-Stone commitments in this audit annex. None supplies a universal abortion formula or automatic burden allocation.

The unchanged neutral/statute premise, provisional and reconciled BSS rows, and narrower-position evidence are preserved in this audit annex. Their source is the version 1.2 record at commits 1d76092/ce8fc4f: its preserved neutral-packet, provisional-all-eight and reconciled-all-eight annexes. Its compatibility and final-join audits supply recorded barriers only, never operative joins or assignments. No BSS component required remodeling. The statutory 90-day reporting period runs from commission of the offense; this precision changes no BSS frozen premise or vote.

J = direct join to the expressly bounded proposition; R = refusal; P = only the named severed proposition is joined; NR = unnecessary independent ground not reached. A stated minimum revision identifies a different compatible public formulation, not a change to Stone's approved text. These granular joins do not imply a whole-framework join when the final-part table records a refusal. The completed section 8 reconciliations govern the stated common-minimum, spousal-notice and Stevens-substantive-formulation refinements.

Additional source keys: F/R/Q/H/M/L/C/W identify the Justice's actual simulated Foucha/Riggins/Quill/Hilton/Medina/Lee/Collins/Wright writings or joins in the unchanged pre-Stone baseline. They provide bounded corroboration, not transplanted abortion holdings. Carey Parts II-III, 431 U.S. 678, 684-690 and n.5, supplies verified entering authority: Blackmun and Stevens joined those parts; Souter applies them through his Payne method. The full CAP primary text, all opinions and notes, was read (https://static.case.law/us/431/cases/0678-01.json; official Reports counterpart https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USREPORTS-431/pdf/USREPORTS-431-678.pdf). The access-specific limit in note 5 excludes a universal rule for every law touching sexual freedom and changes no frozen premise.

## Granular common formulations and proposition tests

**Protected-choice boundary (B, St, So all J).** Before viability a patient may decide to terminate a pregnancy without proving a medical necessity or obtaining official approval of her reasons. The State may regulate competent practice and may not prohibit that protected choice, give a third party effective veto power, or prevent timely treatment necessary for life or health. After viability prohibition remains subject to necessary life-and-health protection. These statements do not immunize demonstrably unsafe methods or resolve a funding/personhood/conscience claim.

**Severe-interference minimum (B, St, So all J at this expressly limited scope, confirmed by the express section 8 reconciliation).** Where a requirement severely interferes with the exercise of protected reproductive choice, it must at a minimum serve a compelling permissible interest and be narrowly tailored. This is a necessary condition, not a sufficient permission: it cannot authorize a prohibition of protected previability choice, an effective third-party veto, or denial of timely necessary life-and-health care. It creates no safe harbor for lesser burdens, does not make strict scrutiny automatic for ordinary consent or limited confidential reporting, and does not replace the remaining precedent applicable to each provision. The causal burden must affect exercise of protected choice, not merely implicate reproductive subject matter.

**Souter's adopted ground:** His frozen SP method retains Roe's fundamental-liberty protection, direct abortion precedents and concrete clinical limits absent special justification. Carey expressly applies the compelling-interest/narrow-drawing requirement to substantial access restrictions, with n.5's important limitation. The circulated language leaves direct precedents and separate results intact, does not make the severe threshold exclusive, allocates no new burden for every lesser interference and undertakes no complete replacement. His express section 8 reconciliation adopts this narrower lawful formulation while resolving the reserved general-articulation question. The strongest objection is that a generic tier may conceal a new full formula and import Riggins into abortion. The limitation to existing protected choice, necessary-only wording and express nonreplacement answer it. No inference is drawn from historical Souter's authorship. If the public formulation instead makes the minimum a complete sufficient standard or abolishes all lesser-burden precedent, Souter refuses and the exact revision above is the minimum needed.

**Precedent-ground common approach.** Apply Akron separately to compulsory adult delay and unnecessary exclusive physician delivery; Doe to protection of timely individualized clinical judgment; Danforth to permissible consent and genuinely confidential relevant reports; the minors' precedents to one-parent structure and effective bypass. A provision can be sustained or invalidated on those grounds without adopting Stone's proposed universal lesser-burden rule. No shared precedent citation erases the separate reporting disagreements.

## Every final opinion part: BSS join, objection and minimum revision

J = join exactly at the published scope, with no further revision required. R = refuse the published ground; the cell states the source objection and minimum revision that would permit a narrower join. NR = leave an unnecessary independent ground unadjudicated; a new sufficient reason to decide it is needed before a merits vote can be inferred. J-descriptive acknowledges the actual Court's separate holdings and does not add an operative vote to a proposition the Justice rejects. All source limitations stated below are conditions of the join.

The four extended explanations have 642 words (protected choice), 638 (governing standard), 679 (stare decisis), and 642 (spousal notice); every other explanation is between 156 and 176 words. Counts concern explanation text, not rule or statutory appendices.

The Blackmun, Stevens and Souter separate summaries are each within 300–500 words and preserve their own framework and component boundaries. Blackmun retains staged scrutiny, rejects mandatory ancillary commands, referral identification and both release duties, while sustaining optional materials and the three medical reports. Stevens's proposed substantive framework is not confused with Court adoption, blanket timetable repeal or Stone's public-release applications. Souter's independent Akron grounds, rejection of a comprehensive replacement, and distinct sustaining referral/public-release applications are explicit. Souter treats the medical-basis reports as documentation of actual lawful judgments. Reporting creates no prior-approval requirement, new testing duty or new offense based on later professional disagreement; underlying statutory and constitutional standards remain. No general professional immunity follows.

## Assignment audit

All 33 final assignment entries were inspected. Their assigners follow the actual judgment coalition, not a presumed historical author or rationale coalition. Souter never receives authorship of a majority rationale he refuses.

- Stone assigns Souter on the protected-choice foundation, stare decisis, necessary minimum/descriptive account, emergency construction/explanation/defense, medical content, each ancillary notice, publication/chosen receipt, basic certification, materials relief, parent structure, incorporated parent content, spousal notice, each medical report, notice reports, marital status, each independent speech part and ancillary certification links. Stone's judgment-only fallback in the independent speech and incorporated-parent-content components still places him in the judgment coalition and permits assignment; it does not supply a rationale signature.
- Stone assigns O'Connor on attendance because he is among the nine supporting that judgment. O'Connor's five-Justice assumed-operation rationale and the four no-established-command concurrences remain distinct. Blackmun, Stevens and Souter's judgment joins do not join her premise.
- White, senior participating Associate Justice within the supporting coalition when Stone is outside, assigns O'Connor on trimester timing, fixed waiting, physician delivery, referral identification, and each timing/delivery certification dependency. Souter joins only the referral sustaining rationale; all three BSS Justices dissent from timing, waiting, delivery and their dependencies.
- White assigns Souter on each public-release provision: Stone is outside the seven-Justice coalition, Souter joins its actual institutional-accountability rationale, and Blackmun's dissent is explicit. Stevens's supporting vote does not entail a join to Stone's contrary application.
- Noncontrolling separate propositions have their stated authors and exact partial joins. Their publication does not create a separate Court assignment in a losing coalition. Souter may author the Akron and no-established-visit separate grounds he actually adopts; Blackmun may publish his own ancillary objection; their shared disposition with another writer does not confer whole-opinion assent.

These assignments rest on the current judgment coalitions and the stated seniority rule. They import no version 1.2 authorship or assignment. Basic certification remains distinct from its disputed dependencies, and Stone's fallback votes remain judgments only.

## Reconciled Stevens substantive-framework join

Stevens's formal join adopts the specified substantive formulation as a supported section 8 refinement of his recorded conditional position. His Thornburgh concurrence protects reproductive choice beyond ordinary economic regulation; his Hodgson analysis puts justification on the State after actual added obstacles and examines each asserted function and less burdensome means; his Webster writing distinguishes clinically useful evaluation from purposeless compulsory costs; his Carey Parts II-III joins support the severe-access minimum. These sources support more than his separately identifiable common-minimum join. The formal whole-substantive-proposal signature is a simulated opinion-level departure from the historical topology, supported by his own sources rather than attributed to historical shared authorship.

The operative conditions are precise. A meaningful State-added burden or demonstrated departure from competent care must be established; professional disagreement or an administrative form alone is insufficient. A proposed alternative must be concrete, practicable, substantially less burdensome and able to serve the same permissible function. The State must answer it, but supported differences in effectiveness, safety or feasibility can supply an answer; the rule does not require the cheapest imaginable law. Clinical evidence and professional agreement carry substantial evidentiary weight without conclusive effect or an association veto, and clinical evidence does not eliminate separately permissible nonclinical interests.

Necessary care remains protected prospectively, without waiting for catastrophe. That protection does not convert every symptom into an emergency, erase the actual section 3203 trigger, or transfer section 3205(c)'s distinct disclosure defense to unrelated duties. Duties must be sufficiently definite and the culpability appropriate to the applicable claim remains necessary; no universal subjective-intent defense or immunity from established fraud, incompetence, malpractice or lawful discipline is adopted. Later professional disagreement alone does not establish wrongdoing. The independent emergency-vagueness and spousal-speech claims remain reserved.

The substantive join applies existing facial and severability principles without a universal probability, numerator, denominator or overbreadth formula. It does not join standalone repeal of the trimester timetable, wholesale displacement of Akron or Thornburgh, or Stone's excluded public-release applications. No judgment changes and no new neutral premise result. The complete substantive proposal has two signatures, Stone and Stevens; the separately adopted common minimum and specific Court holdings retain their own coalitions.

## Completeness and reconciliation result

All 49 opinion parts have an explicit BSS join or refusal, the recorded objection and the minimum revision that would resolve it; all 34 judgment components account for each Justice exactly once. Each published part has unique joiners and includes its author. The 31 holding explanations and all 33 assignments reconcile with those component positions. The Blackmun, Stevens and Souter separate summaries contain 428, 444 and 480 words respectively, and preserve these substantive limits. No unresolved BSS reconciliation issue remains.


# O’Connor and Kennedy — proposition compatibility, opinion joins, judgments and assignments

*Planned Parenthood of Southeastern Pennsylvania v. Casey*, Nos. 91-744 and 91-902; merits and cross-review; effective June 29, 1992; Stone version 1.3. Research cutoff: June 29, 1992. This is single-conversation mode: true blindness was unavailable.

This annex records each Justice’s treatment of the separable propositions, every one of the 49 published opinion parts, all 34 judgment rows and all 33 assignment entries. A join applies only at the stated level of generality. A refusal preserves separately stated narrower positions. Each refusal gives the source-grounded objection and the minimum revision that would resolve it; “none” or an unqualified join means no revision is required. Common labels and matching dispositions establish no additional agreement.

## Refrozen baseline and reconciliation

The unchanged neutral packet, supplied statute and the eight reconciled pre-Stone commitments were reverified and refrozen before Stone’s version 1.3 was opened. The neutral packet and supplied statute are byte-identical to the version 1.2 baseline at ce8fc4f. No changed neutral premise required remodeling either Justice’s row. The historical comparator remains reconciled in that baseline; no post-Stone version 1.2 judgment, assignment, opinion part or final join is carried into this assembly.

O’Connor’s acceptance of explicit narrow tailoring for other proved severe access restrictions is a **bounded §8 refinement**, not an unchanged express historic rule. Her Akron dissent at 467–468 n.11 argues for reasonable relation to a compelling interest and legislative latitude, and that contrary evidence is retained. Her own Carey access analysis at 462–463 supports the refined necessary floor: severity is established before the State’s interests are weighed; genuine safety regulation remains available; no universal cost-minimization duty applies below severity; and satisfying the floor cannot overcome an independent prohibition. No provision judgment changes. Kennedy refuses the generic severe-interference tier because his own Webster, Hodgson and Ohio v. Akron positions establish particular reasonable-regulation and anti-veto rules without selecting that universal sequence.

O’Connor and Kennedy accept the notice-specific qualification of Ohio v. Akron **Part II-A at 514**, which O’Connor joined and Kennedy authored. The compelled group is identified independently of the constitutional conclusion. The reliable findings concern actual adult spousal control, not a speculative malfunction in a minor’s safeguarded judicial bypass. The qualification changes neither Justice’s notice judgment and creates no general facial formula. The two §8 reconciliation audits separately state the strongest contrary evidence and their resolutions.

## Date-eligible authority key

The preserved provisional matrices contain the complete two-path adversarial tests and source-grounded narrower positions. The compatibility tests below preserve those barriers and separately identify the formulation-specific refinements. Each abbreviation identifies a date-eligible writing or join. Historical Casey authorship and joins are not premises of these tests:

- **OA:** O'Connor's Akron dissent, 462 U.S. 416, 452–475 (1983), especially 462–463, 467–468 n.11 and 473–474; severity first, then compelling justification; physician delivery, waiting, disclosure, trimester criticism.
- **OT:** O'Connor's Thornburgh dissent, 476 U.S. 747, 814–832 (1986), especially 828; same threshold approach, evidentiary record and medical-construction limits.
- **OW:** O'Connor's Webster concurrence, 492 U.S. 490, 522–531 (1989), and the Court parts she joined; necessary decision, prudent medical testing, construction and unappealed-scope restraint.
- **OH:** O'Connor's Hodgson concurrence, 497 U.S. 417, 458–461 (1990), and her joins to Stevens's Parts I, II, IV–VII; she refused his general-framework Part III and bypass-rejection Part VIII.
- **OG:** O'Connor's opinion in Mississippi University for Women v. Hogan, 458 U.S. 718 (1982); actual important objective and substantial fit, no stereotyped marital-control entitlement.
- **OM/KM:** O'Connor's Michael H. concurrence, joined by Kennedy, 491 U.S. 110, 132 (1989); no mandatory most-specific-history method.
- **KW:** Webster opinion joined by Kennedy, 492 U.S. 490, especially 518–522 and note 15; retained liberty, rejection of trimester machinery, reasonable medical regulation and physician-delivery criticism.
- **KH:** Kennedy's Hodgson writing, 497 U.S. 417, 480–497 (1990); distinct parental responsibility, adequate bypass, notice/consent distinction, no adult husband control.
- **KO:** Kennedy's Ohio v. Akron opinion, 497 U.S. 502 (1990); bypass and facial discipline. O'Connor joined the Court portions, **including the no-valid-applications passage at page 514 in Part II-A**; she did not join Kennedy's distinct Part V.
- **KP:** Souter's Payne concurrence joined by Kennedy, 501 U.S. 808, 842–856 (1991); special justification beyond constitutional disagreement, demonstrated unworkability and confined overruling.
- **KJ:** Kennedy's Texas v. Johnson concurrence, 491 U.S. 397, 420–421 (1989); genuine expressive protection despite powerful State commitments.
- **R, L, M, C, Q/H, X:** the precise earlier simulated public positions preserved in the baseline: Riggins/Foucha (May 18), Lee (June 24), Medina (June 22), Collins (February 26), Quill/Hilton (May 26/December 16), Hudson/Wright (February 25/June 19). These sources furnish their recorded contextual limits, never a new abortion test by analogy alone.

**Additional authorities:** Carey v. Population Services International, 431 U.S. 678, 686–689 and n.5 (1977), as invoked in O’Connor’s Akron dissent, supplies the access-based distinction; Marks v. United States, 430 U.S. 188, 193 (1977), supplies the judgment-supporting logical-subset inquiry. Act 64 means the Pennsylvania Act of November 17, 1989, P.L. 592, No. 64, particularly its severability provision. District findings and statutory commands are identified separately in the Source Notes.

## Source qualifications incorporated in these join tests

The notice-information permission and the spousal-notice exception remain different rules. Under §3205(a)(2)(iii), **“In the case of rape, this information may be omitted.”** Omission is permitted, not required; it has no police-reporting prerequisite and does not eliminate paternal support liability or guarantee collection. Under §3209’s reported-spousal-sexual-assault route, §3128(c) requires the victim or her agent personally to report to law enforcement with jurisdiction within **90 days of commission of the offense**. District finding 297 explains the reporting obstacle; the clock’s starting point comes from enacted §3128(c), [1984 Act 230, §2, P.L. 1211](https://www.palrb.gov/getfile.cfm?file=resources%2Fpreservation-project%2Fpltiftopdf%2F19001999%2F1984%2F0%2Fact%2F0230.pdf&view=true). It does not begin at discovery of pregnancy or a request for abortion.

Section 3207(b) requires facility name and address, parent/subsidiary/affiliated entity names and addresses, and covered entities sharing contemporaneous ownership, beneficial interest, directorship or officership with another facility, initially within 30 days and updated immediately upon changes. Its public-funding lookback is 12 calendar months **before the inspection or copying request**; without such funding, only law-enforcement officials and the two medical boards receive access for official duties. Section 3214(f)’s quarterly total and trimester reports instead use 12 calendar months **before filing** and remain confidential on a no-funding declaration unless contrary evidence establishes funding. Collection is distinct from public release. Source: the supplied statute, §§3207(b), 3214(f).

Section 3208 requires easily comprehensible English, Spanish and Vietnamese materials, publication within 60 days, annual updating and legible type. Its geographically indexed services directory may be replaced by a toll-free 24-hour number providing the locality’s list and service information. The fetal-development material covers two-week increments from fertilization to full term, probable anatomy and physiology and survival information; pictures state dimensions, are realistic and fit the pregnancy’s stage. Objective, nonjudgmental and scientifically accurate treatment includes abortion methods and risks, possible detrimental psychological effects and childbirth risks. Materials are available free on request in appropriate numbers. The statute’s statements concerning coercion, informed consent/private medical consultation, paternal support and possible adoptive-parent payment remain factual duties with no guarantee of financial availability. Receipt under §3205(a)(3) is chosen; reading and ideological assent are not compelled. Source: supplied §§3205(a)(3)–(4), 3208 and district findings 177–189. These fuller statutory terms confirm the existing premises and change no join or judgment.

## Every provision, independent ground, and remedial component

The complete statutory qualifications are preserved in the neutral-packet verification and Source Notes. Every agreement below includes those terms; a shared disposition does not erase an exception or adopt a different statutory command. In particular rape counseling omission is **permission with no police-report condition**; spousal assault has the distinct personally reported offense within 90 days **of commission**; and the two facility-funding lookbacks differ.

## Controlling-status reconciliation

O’Connor joins the necessary access-based minimum with its express limitations and retains her broader threshold/rational-review method in her separate writing. Kennedy joins the protected boundaries and the accurate account of Court law but refuses the generic severe-interference tier. The minimum has five direct supporters—Stone, Blackmun, Stevens, O’Connor and Souter—while its descriptive account has six, including Kennedy. A different five—White, O’Connor, Scalia, Kennedy and Thomas—displace the trimester timetable as an independent timing restriction. Neither count adopts Stone’s complete replacement or makes his condition on his own timetable agreement binding on the other Justices.

Marks supplies no additional complete formula. Spousal notice has six direct rationale joins. On waiting and physician delivery, Stone, Blackmun, Stevens and Souter oppose sustention; their invalidation rationales cannot provide narrowest grounds for the sustaining judgment. Within that judgment’s actual supporting coalition, O’Connor’s threshold method, Kennedy’s particular reasonable-regulation ground and the three other Justices’ broader rational-review theory do not establish a demonstrated complete logical-subset rule. The five direct joins to the particular permissions control, and the separate necessary minimum controls on its own direct majority.

Certification is counted by dependency: basic receipt nine; mandatory ancillary links eight; fixed-timing links five; physician-delivery links five. Independent medical-speech and chosen-material/basic-certificate speech judgments have nine supporters and eight non-Stone rationale joins. Each independent ancillary-speech judgment has eight supporters and Blackmun’s nonreach, with seven rationale joins. Incorporated parental ancillary content has eight judgment supporters and seven rationale joiners. Stone’s named standing fallback supplies a disposition alone. Parental-attendance relief is denied by nine, with five joining the assumed-operation rationale and four the distinct no-established-command ground.

No O’Connor or Kennedy provision judgment changes from the refrozen baseline. No generic Kennedy commitment changes. The recorded rationale refinements are O’Connor’s explicit tailoring floor and the notice-specific qualification of Ohio v. Akron at the scope stated above. Lucas and Espinosa remain independent same-day events. Casey does not create a constitutional claim Benten’s parties did not present, displace its agency-law questions, or establish entitlement to admission of the drug.


# New version 1.3 compatibility — White, Scalia and Thomas

The operator refroze the unchanged pre-Stone baseline and reused its reconciled commitments before reading version 1.3 in full. These are newly tested severable propositions, not prior signatures. J means direct compatibility only at the stated scope; P means only the stated severed proposition; R means refusal. Every cell states its legal objection and minimum acceptable alternative. A possible alternative is not an invented circulation event or authority to alter Stone. No White, Scalia or Thomas commitment moves. Their independent judgment votes and final opinion signatures are separately recorded.

## Own-writing and current-term authority keys

### White

- **foundation:** White's Doe/Roe dissent, 410 U.S. 221–223, and Thornburgh dissent, 476 U.S. 786–814; his actual Foucha/Riggins joins establish distinct bodily-liberty channels, not an abortion foundation.
- **precedent:** White's Thornburgh dissent and actual Hilton join/Quill Commerce dissent; correction rests on the particular constitutional source and reliance, not membership.
- **consent:** White's Thornburgh dissent and Danforth separate writing; his Riley join, 487 U.S. 781, prevents a paid-speech shortcut.
- **parents:** White's Danforth and Thornburgh separate writings; actual Medina join is bounded corroboration of workable safeguarded procedure.
- **reports:** White's Thornburgh dissent (including its anti-harassment reservation) and Danforth separate writing; actual Foucha/Riggins/Wright positions require exact record and lawful medical responsibility.
- **scope:** White's Danforth severability analysis and actual Wright record-specific position; Riley and the actual argument preserve the separate speech question.

### Scalia

- **foundation:** Scalia's Webster concurrence, 492 U.S. 532–537, Ohio v. Akron concurrence, 497 U.S. 520–521, and Michael H. plurality; his actual Quill concurrence and McCollum dissent supply the adherence counterpath.
- **precedent:** Scalia's Webster concurrence and actual Quill concurrence/McCollum dissent distinguish source error and the congressionally adjustable Commerce precedent.
- **consent:** Scalia's Riley concurrence and Court join except note 11, and Ohio v. Akron concurrence; actual Wright/Riggins limited joins preserve source and factual precision.
- **parents:** Scalia's Ohio v. Akron concurrence and actual Medina/Wright joins; no adult-spouse authority follows from parental responsibility.
- **reports:** Scalia's Riley and Ohio v. Akron writings, plus actual Quill/Wright/Medina joins; clinical reports differ from compelled advocacy and findings cannot be ignored.
- **scope:** Scalia's Michael H. preservation analysis, Ohio v. Akron concurrence and actual Wright join; his Riley writing prevents invented rejection of the separate speech claim.

### Thomas

- **foundation:** Thomas's actual Foucha, Hudson and Riggins dissents, Collins join, McCollum judgment concurrence and Quill join; no date-eligible abortion writing exists. The frozen, bounded source/reliance judgment remains a simulation inference.
- **precedent:** Thomas's actual McCollum concurrence, Quill joins and Wright principal opinion; adherence is a real contrary path, not erased by an assumed historical abortion view.
- **consent:** Thomas's actual Riggins dissent, Collins and Medina joins and Wright principal opinion; Danforth and Riley apply as governing precedents he did not author.
- **parents:** Thomas's actual Medina join, status-sensitive Foucha dissent and Wright opinion; governing minors' precedents apply without inventing an earlier Thomas abortion writing.
- **reports:** Thomas's actual Wright opinion, Riggins dissent, Medina/Quill/Collins joins; governing Danforth permits bounded records while actual interference remains independently examinable.
- **scope:** Thomas's own Riggins scope objection, Wright opinion and McCollum concurrence; governing Riley and the actual argument establish a live source question without proving waiver.

## Common minimum and spousal notice — determinations

**A is supportable as an expressly limited necessary minimum joined by Blackmun, Stevens, O'Connor, and Souter.** It does not establish their agreement on a complete abortion framework. Blackmun and Stevens adopt a recorded narrower position; Souter's explicit acceptance of this particular minimum resolves his reserved formulation question without endorsing a comprehensive replacement. O'Connor's acceptance of the express narrow-tailoring requirement is a supported, bounded refinement that must be recorded as movement, with her contrary *Akron* footnote addressed below. It cannot be described simply as her unchanged historical test.

**B is supportable for Blackmun, Stevens, O'Connor, Kennedy, and Souter at the proposed provision-specific level.** All five already froze a substantive abortion-liberty ground focusing on the women whom the notice requirement actually compels. The express qualification of *Ohio v. Akron*, 497 U.S. 502, 514, must acknowledge that **O'Connor and Stevens joined that passage as well as Kennedy**. The passage is in Part II-A, not the unjoined Part V. The express qualification makes their limited prior commitment explicit; it does not authorize a general abortion facial-challenge formula.

No judgment vote changes on either proposal. This audit supplies no Stone vote, authorship, assignment, or whole-opinion join. Its conclusions are simulation inferences supported by the identified writings and frozen commitments, not facts about an actual circulation or conference.

## A. Necessary minimum for severe interference

### Exact scope audited

Protected previability choice, effective constitutionally required life/health care, and the prohibition of effective third-party veto remain independent protections. Other severe interference with access to protected care must, at minimum, serve a compelling permissible interest and be narrowly tailored. Severity is established before justification. Meeting that minimum does not establish validity; independent prohibitions and retained provision-specific precedent still apply. The proposition neither selects a universal rule for lesser burdens nor converts every serious obstacle into automatic invalidity. It does not itself abandon trimester doctrine or replace the entire governing framework. It sets no universal evidentiary quantum.

“Protected care” cannot be defined retrospectively to mean only care a challenged restriction already permits. Conversely, this minimum does not create a right to an unsafe procedure or decide every postviability risk or method question. “Retained provision-specific precedent” means the precedents and propositions that the Court's actual component decisions leave in force; it is not a device to count every floor joiner as joining every provision disposition or its reasons.

### Source rule

*Carey*, 431 U.S. at 686–690 and n.5, treats access as a means of exercising the protected childbearing decision and applies compelling-interest and narrow-drawing requirements to regulations substantially limiting that access. It is not confined to a direct use prohibition; its analysis expressly discusses restrictions on access to abortion. Footnote 5 excludes an extension to every regulation touching sexual freedom. Part III is an opinion of the Court, joined by Blackmun and Stevens. Stevens expressly confirms his Parts II/III joins in his separate writing; the distinct plurality treatment of minors in Part IV must not be substituted for the adult access rule.

The proposed minimum uses that established access proposition without asserting that *Carey* resolved all later abortion regulation, compelled-speech, minor-consent, medical-risk, or proof questions. It preserves the necessary distinction between the existence of a constitutionally permissible interest, how demanding the justification must be, and whether this particular restriction fits that interest.

### Minimum revisions that resolve objections

The stated A is supported only with every listed reservation. Blackmun needs necessary rather than sufficient protection and preservation of stronger independently applicable law. Stevens needs preservation of meaningful lesser-burden challenges. O'Connor needs factual severity before interests are assessed, possible compelling justification, and no universal least-cost review. Souter needs a named retained access authority and express nonadoption of a comprehensive replacement. These are legal conditions of the joins, not optional explanatory footnotes.

O'Connor's refinement does not silently turn “narrowly tailored” into ordinary rational relationship once severe interference is proved. Nor does it mean that the mere availability of a cheaper rule invalidates any ordinary regulation. A formulation erasing actual tailoring above severity or extending strict review to every smaller burden falls outside the confirmed join.

No *Marks* aggregation is needed to state the proposition if the requisite participating majority actually joins this same text. This audit establishes four non-Stone joins only. It supplies no Kennedy join to A and does not count any Justice's judgment as an unspoken rationale join.

## B. Spousal notice and the facial-review qualification

### Relevant class and precise source treatment

The relevant class is defined independently of the result: married women seeking protected abortion who would not notify voluntarily and whom §3209 actually requires to notify after its operative exemptions. It is **not** defined as only women whom notice ultimately obstructs. The further question is whether practical obstruction is established for a large fraction of that independently defined class. “Large fraction” supplies no invented number or threshold, and “some women” cannot substitute for the record-based magnitude judgment.

The exemptions retain their actual terms: the spouse is not the father; diligent effort cannot locate him; pregnancy results from the specified spousal sexual assault reported by the victim or someone acting for her to competent law enforcement within 90 days of the offense; reason to believe notice likely to cause bodily injury to the woman by her spouse or another person; and the separate medical-emergency exemption. Exception statements are signed, need not be notarized, and carry the punishable-falsity warning. The offense includes intercourse or deviate intercourse obtained through forcible compulsion, a qualifying threat preventing resistance by a person of reasonable resolution, or with an unconscious spouse. Psychological harm, financial withdrawal, divorce or custody retaliation, exposure, and injury to children or others are not generalized exemptions. A nominal bodily-injury exemption cannot be treated as practically available where the credited findings establish an inability to invoke the certification.

The district findings 273–308 and the Third Circuit's affected-population analysis, as frozen in the packet, support practical obstruction and ineffective protection for the compelled class. Most wives' voluntary consultation is not counted as a restrictive application that validates State compulsion of other wives. The record does not establish that every reluctant wife is battered, that all notification is a formal veto, or that any unwelcome conversation is constitutionally severe.

At 497 U.S. 514, *Ohio v. Akron* rejected a facial challenge predicated on a speculative worst-case duration of a functioning minor-bypass scheme. Its no-valid-applications language is in Kennedy's Part II-A, expressly joined by O'Connor and Stevens; it cites O'Connor's *Webster* concurrence at 524. The proposed B **qualifies the reach of that formulation for this demonstrated adult-compulsion setting**. It does not simply pretend the passage never bound or belonged to those Justices. The requirement of more than hypothetical maladministration survives elsewhere. The formal notice/consent distinction also survives; §3209 fails on proved operation, not on an abstract equation of the two.

### Effect of the new public formulation

For all five, B adopts the recorded narrower notice ground and makes the relevant application class and limited precedent treatment explicit. For O'Connor, Stevens, and Kennedy, record the actual prior *Ohio* joinder and the reason its broad formulation is qualified here. If that express qualification is treated as a material refinement of their prior stated scope, this audit confirms its Justice-specific date-eligible basis. None changes the already frozen §3209 judgment or turns a private objection into a new constitutional holding.

The proposed conclusion supports facial relief against §3209 on this record, with the already frozen provision-specific severance and notice/nonnotice-reason reporting consequence. It does not independently invalidate the confidential marital-status inquiry or reopen other reporting. It supplies no automatic consequence for minor-consent bypasses, all waiting periods, all State communications, or unrelated facial challenges.

## Common-minimum and notice authority limits

The two audited grounds may be used only at the exact levels stated above. Their shared protection does not merge Blackmun's stronger framework, Stevens's lesser-burden rule, O'Connor's separate general threshold approach, Kennedy's contextual reservations, or Souter's refusal of comprehensive replacement. Every opinion part retains its separate join test, judgment relationship and assignment basis. No broader claim of controlling law follows from this audit.

## Stevens complete substantive proposal — determination

**Stevens may formally join the proposed complete substantive formulation, at the specified scope.** The formulation adopts his already recorded conditional position: protected previability choice and necessary life/health care, an independent protection against substantial obstacles to protected care, and meaningful review of lesser burdens through actual justification and fit. It preserves the sources of protection that his frozen position required and includes no universal facial formula outside his selected position.

Record this as adoption of a now-specified comprehensive substantive proposal through a supported §8 refinement. It is broader than the separately identified common-minimum join, but it changes none of his frozen judgment votes. The additional specificity concerning alternatives, clinical evidence, sanctions, and implementation is supported only with the boundaries stated below. It neither supplies a standalone repeal of trimester doctrine nor joins the excluded reporting/publication applications. Its controlling status depends on other Justices' actual proposition-level joins, which this audit does not determine.

## Stevens own-writing authority map

- [Stevens, Thornburgh concurrence, 476 U.S. 772–782](https://static.case.law/us/476/cases/0747-01.json): reproductive liberty receives protection beyond ordinary economic regulation; disapproval alone does not transfer the decision to the State; legitimate interests and justified regulation remain possible; constitutional judgment is not reducible to a mechanical formula.
- [Stevens, Hodgson, 497 U.S. 417](https://static.case.law/us/497/cases/0417-01.json), especially Parts III, V–VIII: the State bears justification for actual obstacles; each asserted function is examined; useful one-parent consultation differs from unnecessary second-parent involvement; practical effects and alternatives matter; adult delay is expressly distinguished from the minor-consultation period.
- [Stevens, Webster separate writing, 492 U.S. 560–572](https://static.case.law/us/492/cases/0490-01.json): actual statutory commands cannot be erased by a wished-for construction; medically indicated testing differs from purposeless imposed costs; protection cannot be defeated by a State's preferred theory of life.
- [Carey, 431 U.S. 686–690 and n.5](https://static.case.law/us/431/cases/0678-01.json), Court Parts II–III joined by Stevens: substantially restricted reproductive access requires compelling permissible justification and narrow drawing; the rule does not cover every regulation touching sexual freedom.
- [Stevens, Ohio v. Akron concurrence, 497 U.S. 521–525, and Part II-A join at 514](https://static.case.law/us/497/cases/0502-01.json): effective safeguards and a real implementation record matter; useful reasonable parental notice may survive; hypothetical worst-case operation does not itself warrant facial invalidation; adult counseling precedent remains distinct.

The severe-interference minimum is necessary, not sufficient. It cannot erase independent health, choice or veto protections, or the lesser-burden inquiry below. |
| **Meaningful lesser burden invalid when inadequately justified or fitted; the State substantiates an added condition after a nontrivial access burden or departure from competent practice is established.** | *Hodgson* III expressly places justification on the State after identifying obstacles, and VII–VIII rejects burdens whose useful function is absent even though bypass remains available. *Webster* distinguishes competent testing from a mandatory medically pointless intrusion. His frozen rule selected State justification once a meaningful burden is shown. Counterevidence: he sustains useful limited information, parental protection, and actual confidential records without demanding strict scrutiny of each. | **Join.** The clinical-departure branch concerns a demonstrated State-imposed departure affecting protected care, not a professional association's unsupported disagreement or the bare fact that an administrative form is not itself treatment. A departure triggers an explanation; it does not prove invalidity. Ordinary consent and limited confidential reporting do not automatically receive strict scrutiny. No universal proof quantum is adopted. |
| **The State answers concrete, practicable, substantially less burdensome alternatives serving the same function; no cheapest-imaginable-rule requirement.** | *Hodgson* VII finds that one-parent notice fully serves the legitimate protective function and identifies less burdensome means. VIII refuses an unnecessary court process as a cure for an unjustified underlying rule. His *Ashcroft* join distinguishes useful written reasons from unnecessary second-physician intervention and examines unjustified professional costs. Counterevidence: *Hodgson* VI sustains a reasonable consultation period despite a finding that a shorter period could serve some purpose. | **Join as a supported specification of his recorded fit inquiry.** The alternative must be concrete, workable, substantially less burdensome, and capable of serving the same legitimate function. The State must answer it, but need not select the cheapest imaginable approach. A supported difference in effectiveness, safety, feasibility or other relevant function may answer it. The formulation does not mechanically invalidate every rule once an expert proposes a marginally cheaper one. |
| **Substantial weight for relevant clinical evidence and professional agreement, without an association veto.** | His *Webster* opinion uses medical facts to distinguish indicated testing from useless compulsory procedures while retaining the court's interpretive responsibility. His *Thornburgh* majority join protects individualized informed care; his *Ashcroft* join tests the actual medical usefulness of added requirements. Counterevidence: none gives a professional organization power to determine constitutionality, and parental/accountability interests are not reducible to clinical benefit. | **Join as evidentiary guidance, not a new conclusive presumption.** Reliable relevant professional evidence matters materially. Judges still identify the law, assess disagreement and decide constitutional justification. Clinical evidence does not by itself refute a separately permissible nonclinical interest. No organizational veto or fixed weight is created. |
| **Timely good-faith physical and mental clinical judgment; no requirement to await catastrophe.** | His *Thornburgh* majority join protects maternal health and individualized care; *Webster* recognizes appropriate medical evaluation. His frozen §3203 row sustains the prospective good-faith construction protecting serious threats at onset and expressly anticipates fresh review of harmful later narrowing. Counterevidence: the same row rejects treating every minor or transient symptom as a statutory emergency and refuses rewriting the statute. | **Join at the necessary-care level stated.** Prospective risk assessment remains prospective; failure of the feared injury to materialize does not retroactively make a reasonable assessment unlawful. The clause does not invent an exemption for every claim of distress, change the actual §3203 trigger, or convert §3205(c)'s separate information defense into a general exemption from waiting or other duties. Reserved degrees of risk and unrelated postviability questions remain reserved. |
| **Sufficiently definite duties and appropriate culpability; later professional disagreement alone is not wrongdoing; fraud, malpractice and lawful discipline remain available.** | *Webster* demands fidelity to actual legal duties; his frozen medical-basis and emergency-report rows preserve good faith and reject liability merely because an assessed risk did not occur. The serious counterevidence is the explicit frozen decision to leave standalone emergency vagueness and its preservation undecided. Neither the source set nor the frozen row supplies a universal subjective-intent defense to every medical law. | **Join only in its stated general, protective scope; that scope is compatible with the proposal.** The clause recognizes the need for lawful notice and the culpability required by the applicable claim; it does not announce that all sanctions require the same mental state. Later disagreement alone cannot supply wrongdoing, while incompetence, fraud, malpractice or otherwise established violations remain examinable. No separate merits ruling on §3203 vagueness, waiver, or a new immunity follows. |
| **Truthful correction, no ideological compulsion; proportionate severed relief under applicable existing facial precedent.** | *Thornburgh*, *Carey* and Stevens's *Riley* join protect choice and expression against compelled ideology. His frozen information rows sustain narrow truthful clinical and option notices, and his *Ohio* concurrence accepts useful facially adequate safeguards. *Webster* and *Hodgson* distinguish provisions and remedies. Counterevidence: he expressly reserved standalone spousal speech and did not select a universal abortion facial formula. | **Join.** The proposal does not make every truthful fact compulsory or every compulsory fact ideological; actual content, function and burden matter. Retain the separate spousal-speech and preservation reservation. Apply the relevant established facial and severability rules; no universal probability, numerator, denominator, or overbreadth formula is introduced. |

## Stevens — basis for the supported adoption

The frozen Stevens handoff already contemplated a concrete framework that preserves choice, viability and health; independently protects against substantial obstacles; scrutinizes meaningful lesser burdens; places justification on the State; and evaluates real fit and less burdensome means. The present formulation supplies those terms. His *Hodgson* analysis demonstrates the essential distinction: the State can justify useful parental consultation, but an additional family intrusion that does not serve that function remains objectionable even if a court procedure permits eventual access. His *Webster* writing supplies the parallel clinical distinction between appropriate tests and purposeless compulsory requirements. His *Thornburgh* concurrence supplies the constitutional reason that mere preference cannot answer either defect.

The proposal also answers his strongest concerns about overgeneralization. It does not use ordinary cost as an automatic invalidity trigger, give medical organizations final authority, treat every delay as State-caused, confer immunity from valid clinical regulation, or use a new universal facial formula to decide every provision. Its practical-alternative requirement asks for an answer to a serious alternative, preserving the possibility that the State can demonstrate a relevant difference. Its clinical branch requires an established departure affecting protected care and genuine analysis of the added condition, not ritual invocation of professional custom. These are substantive limits on the join.

The complete formulation is therefore a supported formal adoption of his recorded conditional position, with material articulation of its implementation. It is not attributable to him merely because another Justice proposed it, and the preexisting common-minimum join alone would not authorize it. This audit separately confirms his own sources for the expanded adoption. No new facts or changed entering-law premise were found requiring a neutral packet rebuild.

## Stevens — historical reconciliation

The authorized comparator reconciliation records that historical Stevens did not join the trio's entire general framework. It also records his own recognition that a burden may be objectionable for its severity or its inadequate justification and his insistence that lesser unjustified delay remains objectionable. That comparison corroborates his independent frozen meaningful-burden method. It does not establish that he historically signed this detailed substantive formulation, accepted a universal facial rule, or abandoned all trimester protections.

**New historical departure to record:** the simulated formal join to this complete substantive proposal is a different opinion-level/general-framework commitment from the historical topology. Its basis is Stevens's *Hodgson* burden/justification and actual-fit analysis, *Thornburgh* reproductive-liberty explanation, *Webster* clinical/text distinctions, and *Carey* access-rule join, together with the preserved operative qualifications. His independently frozen departures concerning particular disclosure/reporting applications remain as previously reconciled; this audit does not revise them. His comparison with history must be reported as a supported inference, not historical fact or inevitable behavior.

## Stevens — precise join scope and consequences

1. Record Stevens's **formal join to this substantive proposal**, identifying its exact section or propositions. The common-minimum join remains narrower and independently identifiable.
2. Keep all Stevens judgment votes unchanged. A full substantive-framework join does not adopt the excluded public-report applications or alter his separate provision analysis.
3. Do not count this join as a standalone repeal of trimester doctrine, wholesale overruling of *Akron* or *Thornburgh*, a new universal facial test, or an independent equality, general privacy, spousal-speech or emergency-vagueness holding.
4. Preserve the required boundaries within the joined writing. In particular, “appropriate culpability” is not a universal intent rule, a clinical departure is not conclusive invalidity, and “no catastrophe wait” does not erase the actual emergency trigger or create an every-symptom exception.
5. The confirmed join does not extend to any of those excluded propositions or to a formulation that removes the stated substantive safeguards; a materially broader formulation requires a separate join test.

**Reconciliation status:** The common-minimum, spousal-notice, and complete Stevens substantive-proposal determinations are preserved with their stated limits. No broader legal conclusion or coalition is supplied.

## Every final judgment component

| Component | White | Scalia | Thomas | Stone | Ground and remedy check |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| §3203 — emergency definition | Supports stated disposition | Supports stated disposition | Supports stated disposition | Supports stated disposition | Affirm rejection of facial emergency-definition relief under the stated construction; ordinary conforming mandate, with no separate vagueness remedy. |
| §3205(b) — emergency explanation | Supports stated disposition | Supports stated disposition | Supports stated disposition | Supports stated disposition | Affirm sustention of the emergency explanation requirement with its express if-possible qualification; no special injunction or remand. |
| §3205(c) — separate disclosure-health defense | Supports stated disposition | Supports stated disposition | Supports stated disposition | Supports stated disposition | Retain the defense exactly as enacted; no new waiting or emergency exception is created. |
| §3205(a)(1)(i)–(iii) — medical content | Supports stated disposition | Supports stated disposition | Supports stated disposition | Supports stated disposition | Affirm the content disposition; preserve accuracy, materiality and the disclosure-health defense. |
| §3205(a)(1) — physician-only oral delivery | Supports stated disposition | Supports stated disposition | Supports stated disposition | Opposes stated disposition | Affirm; no injunction against the actual physician-delivery duty; preserve (a)(2) delegation. |
| §3205(a)(1)–(2) — fixed 24-hour interval | Supports stated disposition | Supports stated disposition | Supports stated disposition | Opposes stated disposition | Affirm; no injunction against the actual interval; emergency protection remains. |
| §3205(a)(2)(i) — materials-availability notice | Supports stated disposition | Supports stated disposition | Supports stated disposition | Supports stated disposition | Affirm; no compulsory acceptance, reading or endorsement. |
| §3205(a)(2)(ii) — possible-assistance notice | Supports stated disposition | Supports stated disposition | Supports stated disposition | Supports stated disposition | Affirm; no benefits guarantee. |
| §3205(a)(2)(iii) — paternal-support notice | Supports stated disposition | Supports stated disposition | Supports stated disposition | Supports stated disposition | Affirm; omission permitted in rape without police-report prerequisite; liability is not guaranteed payment. |
| §3208 and §3205(a)(3) — publication and chosen receipt | Supports stated disposition | Supports stated disposition | Supports stated disposition | Supports stated disposition | Affirm; concrete unlawful implementation remains challengeable. |
