This is not a generalized secrecy entitlement. R/L reinforce real State interference. | Refuse a universal rule that spouses may never be required to disclose legally relevant information. Minimum: private reproductive communication as a prerequisite to protected medical choice, with this coercive record. |
| Spousal equal-protection ground | A: pregnancy’s biological difference and a father’s interest justify asymmetric notice. B: the law additionally allocates a marital entitlement to husbands and an affirmative medical-choice burden to wives without adequate fit, beyond biological classification. | **Join narrow independently sufficient sex-equality invalidation.** OG requires persuasive important-objective/substantial-fit justification and rejects stereotyped roles; OHS separates actual parental responsibility from imposed control. The State has not connected compulsory disclosure in these relationships to a legitimate equality-consistent marital goal strongly enough; biological difference does not authorize a husband’s supervisory entitlement. R/C require this distinct State allocation, not a claim all pregnancy rules are sex discrimination. | Refuse a holding that every pregnancy classification triggers the same result, or that fatherhood has no legitimate interests. Minimum: the asymmetric adult marital-control condition, applying Hogan’s fit analysis and this record. |
| Spousal compelled-speech theory — independent reach | A: reach a sufficiently preserved First Amendment objection because the State conditions treatment on a wife’s communication of an intimate fact, regardless of the separate abortion-liberty doctrine. B: leave the independent speech theory and its disputed preservation undecided because the selected liberty/privacy/equality grounds already afford complete notice relief. | **B. No independent spousal First Amendment holding; no merits rejection or waiver ruling.** OA/OT identify genuine compelled-ideology concerns, so the argument is not dismissed merely because the communication concerns medical care. OW’s necessary-decision restraint nevertheless controls: the actual statute does not prescribe a personally uttered ideological formula, and this case needs no additional general compelled-communication rule after notice is invalidated on the selected grounds. Kolbert’s Tr.51–52 argument establishes oral presentation; O’Connor’s Tr.36–38 questions do not establish a vote or settle preservation. C/X require a distinct source and exact reach. | Refuse a statement that spousal speech was never argued, that the theory was conclusively waived, or that the Court decided all spousal notification duties constitutional under the First Amendment. Minimum: acknowledge the distinct argued theory, preserve its independent merits/preservation questions, and provide full relief on the adopted grounds. |
| Independent speech: medical core | A: treat licensed professional speech as wholly commercial and freely compellable. B: recognize First Amendment protection but sustain accurate material medical information necessary to informed treatment. | **Reject the independent facial speech challenge on B’s narrow ground.** OA/OT reserve ideological compulsion but distinguish truthful informed consent. The providers did not concede all speech commercial. R protects informed choice; L does not transform ordinary information into coerced ideological assent. | Refuse blanket commercial-speech classification or immunity from First Amendment review. Minimum: factual, relevant medical disclosure without required endorsement. |
| Independent speech: materials notice, assistance, paternal support, chosen copy, certification | A: invalidate each as a compulsory pro-childbirth message. B: distinguish factual availability/liability notices, chosen receipt and receipt certification from adopting State ideology. | **Reject facial speech relief for each listed component separately.** OA/OT’s possible compelled-ideology concern receives an answer: no requirement to assert a moral belief, endorse an agency, guarantee assistance/collection, read unchosen material or assent. Some listed-agency defects do not change what the speaker must say. Omission in rape remains permitted, without reporting. L/C supply the boundary against viewpoint-based attribution alone. | Refuse approval of compelled ideological or demonstrably false content. Minimum: each precise factual notice and receipt act, physician disagreement/correction allowed, patient choice respected. |
| Referrer identity, §3214(a)(1) | A: invalidate because two doctors would stop referrals even with confidentiality and referral identity has little medical value. B: sustain identification of a participant who may furnish informed consent/gestational information and permit follow-up. | **Sustain the appealed referrer field.** OT demanded evidence rather than speculation; this record does establish limited referral refusal, but not severe access loss or irrationality of identifying participating medical sources. OW/OA distinguish cost/deterrence from undue burden. C prevents private reluctance alone from becoming an absolute constitutional immunity. | Refuse denial of the two-doctor finding or public disclosure of individual reports. Minimum: confidential identity for legitimate follow-up/enforcement, without declaring every conceivable source-identification demand valid. |
| Medical-necessity basis, §3214(a)(8) | A: invalidate because post24-week necessity judgments are chilled by retrospective scrutiny. B: sustain documenting why §3211(b)(1)’s necessity predicate was invoked. | **Sustain.** OT permits legitimate confidential records and professional accountability; OW allows useful regulation of medical judgment. Asking the physician’s basis does not itself change the substantive necessity rule or establish punishment for a reasonable decision. R/M distinguish a record requirement from moving every substantive proof burden. | Refuse characterization as a generic viability result or validation of all §3211 restrictions. Minimum: document this specific invoked predicate, retain clinical/legal safeguards and confidential handling. |
| Emergency basis, §3214(a)(10) | A: invalidate because documenting emergency may deter timely care. B: sustain retrospective documentation without requiring permission or delaying treatment. | **Sustain under the prospective emergency construction.** OA/OT/OW support medical regulation short of actual severe interference. No finding establishes that this confidential aftercare report itself prevents necessary care. R preserves substantive health protection. | Refuse preauthorization, immediate paperwork before treatment, or a narrower emergency definition. Minimum: after-the-fact basis for the actual exemption, without changing good-faith clinical discretion. |
| Diagnostic basis, §3214(a)(11) incorporating §3210(a) | A: invalidate intrusive judgment scrutiny despite unchallenged gestational-age result. B: sustain reporting actual inquiries/tests and basis under a prudent-physician standard. | **Sustain the appealed diagnostic-basis report.** OW’s useful, prudent testing is the closest anchor; OT opposes presumed invalidity of confidential medical documentation. This does not order additional unnecessary tests or reopen the sustained age-result field. R/C preserve the source and scope distinction. | Refuse conflation with(a)(5), fixed mandated tests, or loss of the emergency-prevents-compliance qualification. Minimum: actual prudent diagnostic process and basis only. |
| Notice-linked report, §3214(a)(12) | A: retain all information because reporting is independently useful. B: remove notice/nonnotice-reason fields which perpetuate the invalid disclosure condition; preserve separable marital-status collection. | **Sever notice and nonnotice-reason requirements; retain the marital-status field within otherwise unchallenged confidential collection.** OA/OT permit health data, while OH/OHS do not permit evasion of the substantive decision by a report demanding the same protected explanation. X supports separating the fields. | Refuse automatic invalidation of all marital statistics or compulsory reasons for exercising the right to withhold spousal disclosure. Minimum: marital status alone, no notice-compliance enforcement. |
| Public facility/affiliation access, §3207(b) | A: invalidate because real harassment fears induce funding refusal and likely harm indigent access. B: sustain public accountability for facilities receiving State funds; no patient identity is exposed and incremental severe access effect is not demonstrated. | **Sustain public release on this record.** OW’s funding holdings and OA/OT’s access threshold permit a rational transparency condition. The full findings of harassment and funding refusal are accepted; they do not establish the needed severe causal effect of these particular public reports. This is not a declaration that every funding condition is valid. C requires the condition’s actual operation. | Refuse conflation with §3214(f)’s filing lookback or denial of harassment evidence. Minimum: facility/affiliation data with the12months-before-request trigger; collection remains separately lawful. |
| Public quarterly totals, §3214(f) | A: invalidate because disclosure could amplify harassment and funding covers services beyond abortions. B: sustain aggregate accountability for a recipient of State funds without patient identification. | **Sustain separately.** OW and OA/OT support rational transparency absent severe demonstrated incremental obstruction. Minimum: aggregate totals/trimester report with12months-before-filing trigger and contrary-evidence rule. |
| Unappealed confidential collection/gestational ascertainment | A: reopen the entire scheme because framework changes. B: respect providers’ failure to cross-appeal the district-sustained items and the limited public-release challenge. | **Leave unappealed collection and prudent gestational ascertainment in place; do not newly adjudicate every item.** OW’s necessary-decision rule is direct; OT’s procedural caution and X prohibit expanding the case through generic labels. | Refuse a new omnibus constitutional holding or manufactured claim. Minimum: identify untouched scope and decide only appealed fields/dependencies. |
| Severance, mandate and conditional alternative-theory remand | A: strike the whole Act or remand every alternative constitutional foundation merely because the trimester rules change. B: sever invalid notice-related duties, affirm the other appealed dispositions on the grounds above and remand for conforming relief. | **B.** OW/OT favor limited necessary adjudication; retained constitutional choice removes the providers’ stated contingency for a wholesale remand of alternative foundations. Independently developed speech/equality/privacy grounds receive the treatment recorded above. Act64 severability permits unaffected provisions/applications to operate. Minimum: precise notice/dependent-report relief and ordinary conforming proceedings. |

## Kennedy — framework and grounds frozen before any proposed writing

| Component | Two lawful paths and strongest competing case | Selected commitment, own authority and continuity | Join barrier and minimum narrower position |
|---|---|---|---|
| Protected constitutional choice | A: because Roe is controversial and constitutionally debatable, replace it with ordinary legislative choice. B: retain the established due-process liberty while resolving the particular restrictions. | **B. Retain constitutional protection for the previability decision and reject comprehensive extinguishment of that choice.** KW expressly recognizes liberty and leaves Roe’s central holding undisturbed; KM rejects a mechanically narrow history rule; KP requires special justification beyond disagreement. No demonstrated defect in the central prohibition rule supplies it here. R/C respect defined constitutional channels. | Refuse a declaration of no constitutional protection or wholesale endorsement of Roe’s implementation. Minimum: protected choice survives; particular regulations receive separate examination. |
| Trimester implementation | A: retain the rigid calendar because it secures the choice. B: replace it because it makes medical details constitutional rules and wrongly confines potential-life interests to later pregnancy. | **B.** KW is explicit, including criticism of delivery distinctions and intricacy; KH/KO permit meaningful minor regulation. Q/H demonstrate that correcting implementation need not erase a distinct core. | Refuse a rule that all previability potential-life regulation is forbidden or that medicine’s calendar alone selects scrutiny. Minimum: legitimate interests throughout pregnancy, subject to the protected decision. |
| Viability and health | A: erase viability entirely because KW criticizes its role in the framework. B: retain the operative choice/prohibition distinction while permitting reasonable earlier regulation; preserve medical life/health protection. | **B, limited to the retained governing boundary.** KW distinguishes rejection of a rigid regulatory timetable from reopening Roe’s comprehensive-ban holding and sustains medically useful testing. This does not decide every postviability restriction. R shows that medical liberty requires its own precise channel. | Refuse to equate potential-life interest with a power to extinguish previability choice, or to approve all later restrictions. Minimum: regulatory interests can precede viability; the retained protected decision remains real. |
| General burden framework | A: announce a comprehensive new substantial-obstacle test for every regulation. B: retain a narrower rule: reasonable measures furthering legitimate interests are permissible when they preserve effective choice; a State may not create an effective third-party veto, and demonstrated serious interference requires analysis against the particular protected right. | **B.** KW never adopts a universal undue-burden formula; KH’s no-absolute-obstacle reasoning is tied to minor/parent authority and safeguards. R/Foucha/M insist that one setting’s test not migrate without justification. The present judgments can be resolved without freezing a new universal burden scale. | **Cannot join an unqualified general formula merely bearing “undue burden” or “substantial obstacle.”** Can join protected choice, reasonable nonpreclusive regulation and the specific anti-veto rule. Broader agreement would require a recorded reconciliation explaining the actual new proposition. |
| Smaller meaningful burdens, fit and proof | A: place State proof of adequate justification/fit on every meaningful burden. B: sustain reasonable nonpreclusive regulation without turning all cost or discouragement into heightened review. | **B.** KW expressly accepts useful costs and regulated medical judgment; KH rejects perfect-fit demands and KO rejects hypothetical administrative worst cases. Riggins’s extraordinary trial showing and M’s State procedural latitude are both context-specific. | Refuse a universal meaningful-burden evidentiary shift or least-restrictive-means requirement. Minimum: genuine reasonable relationship, actual record effects and independent constitutional limits. |
| Severe obstacles and State interests | A: declare any substantial obstacle automatically invalid under all circumstances. B: distinguish extinguishing the protected decision or giving another person control from a genuine health regulation needing its own analysis. | **B. The effective third-party veto here is forbidden; no universal automatic-invalidity rule is selected for every severe medical regulation.** KW’s medically prudent construction and KH’s safeguards make the distinction necessary. Mere potential-life preference cannot explain an external veto over the retained choice. R/M supply a methodological check only. | Refuse a formulation which silently decides every serious health regulation. Minimum: this anti-veto rule and justified, nonpreclusive regulation; a broader general test is an unresolved doctrinal choice, not a frozen joinder. |
| Purpose and independent rights | A: treat childbirth encouragement as sufficient proof of impermissible purpose, or license any regulation with that purpose. B: accept truthful encouragement while separately enforcing protected choice and genuine speech/privacy limits. | **B.** KW allows a governmental preference; KJ shows strong public commitments cannot defeat an independently established constitutional command. KH protects family participation for a particular legitimate reason, not at any cost. L distinguishes actual pressure from mere offense. | Refuse either categorical anti-persuasion or categorical immunity. Minimum: identify the precise message, effect and constitutional source. |
| Facial proof/operative population | A: voluntary notice by most wives defeats relief under broad facial-challenge language. B: the challenged legal compulsion operates on those who would not notify; its proven control cannot be diluted by unaffected relationships. | **B for spousal compulsion, with KO’s ordinary facial discipline retained elsewhere.** KH’s distinction between minors and adults and its reliance on usable safeguards mean its ordinary notice defense does not decide this case. L’s public pressure ground rejects formal freedom when State conditions make it unreal. C supplies affirmative State attribution. | Refuse a general “one hard case is enough” rule or a denial that KO requires more than hypothetical maladministration. Minimum: actual defined condition, proved operative class, tailored relief. |
| Stare decisis | A: constitutional error alone permits repudiation; or all Roe applications are inseparable. B: require special justification and determine which component its evidence reaches. | **B.** KP expressly requires special justification; KW demonstrates one for trimester machinery while leaving the core. H’s separable statutory holding and Q’s precise reliance-based adherence confirm methodological consistency but are not direct constitutional analogues. Settled ability to order intimate life supports keeping the core; that is an inference from the protected legal arrangement and advocates’ argument, not a new trial finding. | Refuse error-only overruling, immutable precedent, or a separate rule making controversy itself decisive. Minimum: worked defect and scope, respect for settled liberty, no invented quantitative reliance or institutional history. |

## Kennedy — each separable provision and alternative ground

| Component | Two lawful paths and strongest counterargument | Frozen disposition and concrete sufficient ground | Join barrier; minimum narrower formulation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Medical emergency, §3203/dependent exemptions | A: invalidate because only state courts can finally settle the definition and some health risks remain outside it. B: sustain prospective good-faith clinical treatment of serious risk and the three diagnoses without waiting for damage. | **Sustain as construed.** KW construes testing to avoid dangerous/irrelevant procedures and preserves clinical judgment; KO accepts workable construction rather than worst-case assumptions. A later contrary authoritative construction remains a new problem. R/M reject shifting a different procedure’s rule here. | Refuse catastrophe-first enforcement or claiming federal interpretation binds state courts permanently. Minimum: operative prospective construction and preserved challenge to materially different enforcement. |
| Emergency vagueness — threshold and merits reach | A: affirm a standalone vagueness rejection based on the physician’s good-faith clinical judgment and prospective construction. B: resolve the developed construction/health issue without deciding an additional constitutional theory whose independent preservation/necessity is disputed. | **B. Do not reach an independent vagueness merits holding; grant no additional vagueness relief.** KW’s refusal to decide unnecessary constitutional questions and KO’s attention to the actual statutory challenge control the reach decision. The district did not decide vagueness and the Third Circuit rejected it, but the providers’ developed argument here principally concerns health protection and the saving construction. Neither lower-court history nor a governmental waiver assertion creates a new fully litigated Supreme Court holding. C/X preserve the distinction between affirming the practical disposition and adopting every lower-court rationale. | Refuse a manufactured concession/waiver ruling or categorical immunity for statutes employing medical judgment. Minimum: sustain the construction on the developed ground, acknowledge the appellate vagueness treatment, and reserve a separate vagueness merits rule. |
| Emergency explanation and separate information defense | A: strike possible interference with urgent care; B: enforce the explanation only before abortion **if possible** and the separate severe-adverse-health reasonable-belief/preponderance defense as written. | **Sustain these bounded provisions.** KW’s clinical-construction method and KO’s practical statutory reading apply. Neither requirement creates prior permission for emergency treatment, and the information defense does not supply a general waiting waiver. R protects actual medically necessary intervention. | Refuse a new defense broader than text or emergency care conditioned on paperwork. Minimum: distinct functions and precise terms; no compelled postponement. |
| Medical-information core, §3205(a)(1)(i)–(iii) | A: preserve Akron/Thornburgh’s categorical restriction on structured dialogue. B: sustain relevant procedure, risk/alternative, gestational-age and childbirth information. | **Sustain content.** KW directly criticizes exceptional invalidation of informed-consent regulation; KO recognizes informed medical participation. The patient’s retained liberty is consistent with information rather than physician insulation. R/C require this specific medical relationship. | Refuse false or irrelevant content, compulsory ideological assent, or a conflation with timing/delivery. Minimum: accurate relevant informed-consent facts. |

| Materials-availability notice, §3205(a)(2)(i) | A: invalidate mandatory referral to a State persuasion program with defective directory entries. | Assistance notice, §3205(a)(2)(ii) | A: condemn one-sided encouragement or an illusory benefits promise. | Paternal-support notice, §3205(a)(2)(iii) | A: invalidate because actual support may be unavailable and rape counseling may cause harm. B: sustain truthful documentation of valid disclosures and chosen receipt. | **Sustain.** KW permits informed-consent administration; KJ would resist ideological endorsement, which this certification does not require. | Fixed24-hour interval | A: invalidate actual travel, repeated visits, extended scheduling, expense and risk under Akron. ## Freeze summary for later coalition work

### Explicit health-boundary and proposition-count clarification

The framework rows retain Roe’s governing limit on postviability proscription: abortion necessary, in appropriate medical judgment, to preserve the woman’s life or health remains constitutionally protected. They do **not** newly adjudicate every degree of medical risk, every method-selection dispute, all §3211 restrictions, or every postviability regulation. O’Connor’s OT expressly reserved when a health/fetal-survival tradeoff becomes undue after construing the particular risk as real and identifiable; nothing in this freeze silently closes that reservation. Kennedy’s KW used a construction avoiding medically irrelevant or dangerous testing, without adopting a universal risk-calibration rule. Both accept the prospective emergency construction described in their provision rows; neither treats the separate information-omission defense as a substitute for timely emergency care. The governing source is the retained Roe proposition as discussed/applied in their own OW/KW writings, with OT’s express reservation, rather than a new factual finding or a wholesale joinder to Roe’s reasons.

Each reusable proposition must receive its own express count at assembly. These two Justices’ support for protected previability choice and the retained life/health limit can be counted only at that exact level; their matching dispositions on many regulations cannot be counted as joinders to a shared comprehensive framework. O’Connor’s severity-then-compelling-justification approach and Kennedy’s selected narrower contextual rules are different rationales. Neither is automatically a logical subset of the other merely because both sustain the same provisions here. Any eventual Marks analysis must show the actual rationales and entailment across their covered cases; this freeze supplies no default Marks conversion. The extended holdings on protected choice, postdecision regulatory standard, stare decisis and spousal notice must separately state their proposition supporters, actual controlling status and reserved breadth. No opinion-majority count follows from the judgment table alone.

**O’Connor:** sustain the appealed emergency/information/delivery/waiting/parental/reporting/public-release provisions on the precise grounds above; invalidate spousal notice and notice/nonnotice-reason reporting, preserving marital status. Independently supports the narrow spousal protected-choice, adult-family-privacy and sex-equality grounds. Retains constitutional choice, rejects trimester machinery, and selects her actual severe-burden-then-possible-compelling-justification framework with rational review below severity. She does not select meaningful-burden balancing or automatic invalidation of every substantial obstacle.

**Kennedy:** same specified provision dispositions, but not identical rationales. Retains protected choice, rejects trimester machinery and permits reasonable nonpreclusive regulation. Invalidates the actual State-enabled third-party control; does not yet select a universal undue-burden formula, automatic obstacle rule or meaningful-burden burden shift. Spousal decision autonomy is sufficient; a broader standalone informational-privacy rule and independently sufficient equal-protection holding remain expressly undecided. These are bounded doctrinal reservations, not missing judgment votes.

**No authorship or coalition assumption:** neither a joint opinion nor any author, assigned role, full-opinion joinder or opinion majority follows from these commitments. A proposed circulation must be tested proposition by proposition against the actual limits above. If a broader general formulation moves either Justice, the record must explain the new sufficient ground, the source and the reconciliation before freezing that change; a shared disposition or familiar label does not suffice.

**Pre-comparator scope-refresh reconciliation:** The validated spousal-speech addendum required express reach rows, not a change to any selected provision disposition or framework proposition. Both Justices leave the independent spousal-speech merits and preservation questions undecided because their own adopted grounds supply complete relief. Emergency-vagueness rows likewise identify nonreach of an independent merits/waiver holding. These clarifications were completed and refrozen before comparator or Stone access; no historical result supplied the choices.

**Parental-content clarification, before global freeze:** Both Justices’ parental-consent sustention treats the district court’s use of §3205 information to explain informed-parent content at744F.Supp.1382–1384 as a lower-court construction; it does not invent an express §3206 incorporation of every §3205 mechanism, a separate parent-specific24-hour waiting period, or a nondelegable physician-only parental-delivery command, and it leaves the distinct attendance findings and Third Circuit note23’s reserved interpretation exactly as identified above.

# Casey v1.2 — provisional Blackmun, Stevens, and Souter commitments

**Stage: FROZEN BEFORE HISTORICAL COMPARATOR AND BEFORE STONE TEXT.** September 15, 2026. Effective-law cutoff June 29, 1992 immediately before Casey. This is the Engine's disclosed single-conversation fallback with scoped source handoffs, not a claim of blindness. The operator who prepared these rows read the neutral record and entering public law; no historical Casey opinion, runtime comparator, Stone Section II, prior Casey record, or prior modeling was opened. The user's task description itself disclosed drafting concepts. It supplies no Justice's vote, assignment, or joinder.

The controlling neutral source is `neutral-modeling-packet.md`, frozen before modeling. Its entire statutory text, exceptions, provenance distinctions, lower-court full-read reports, and briefs/argument record are incorporated. This matrix identifies conclusions and legal reasons, not invented conference discussion or draft history. Each row independently tests two legally available paths. A candidate formulation that crosses a recorded barrier requires the Engine's reconciliation audit; it cannot be called confirmation. A newly discovered material source fact requires neutral refresh and affected refreeze before comparison.

## Sources and full-read gate

This modeler personally read Blackmun's full Webster separate opinion, Blackmun's full Ashcroft separate opinion and Ohio v. Akron dissent; Stevens's full Thornburgh concurrence, Webster separate opinion, Hodgson writing (all parts, statutory appendix and notes), Ohio v. Akron concurrence, and short Riley separate writing; and Souter's full Payne concurrence including notes. Root independently read the full Blackmun Roe and Thornburgh majority opinions including all notes; the bounded report `blackmun-roe-thornburgh-source-report.md` was read and incorporated before this freeze. The source packet's full Third Circuit opinion was read by this modeler; the full district opinion and all merits briefs and argument were read by designated source agents/root with reports in the packet. Full-read status is not inferred from a citation or extract. All opinion texts are fresh or source-validated CAP primary texts in `prior/` and `authorities/`.

Source keys below are exact writings, not whole-case labels:

- **BR**: Blackmun, Roe majority, 410 U.S. 113, especially 152–165 and paternal-right footnote; January 22, 1973. The abortion choice is protected Fourteenth Amendment liberty/privacy; distinct maternal-health/potential-life interests become compelling at different stages; postviability regulation must preserve life and health. No decision when life begins or on paternal rights.
- **BT**: Blackmun, Thornburgh majority, 476 U.S. 747, especially 759–771 and its notes; June 11, 1986. Stevens joined. Ordinary voluntary informed consent is valid; mandatory indiscriminate discouragement and irrelevant information are different. Confidential health reporting is permissible; public individual reporting that risks identifying the woman is not. The then-unresolved facility-publication and parental-operation issues are not prior holdings. The former paternal-support provision lacked today's rape omission permission. The older scheme lacked today's severability clause.
- **BW**: Blackmun, Webster separate, 492 U.S. 490, 537–560; July 3, 1989. Retains Roe's framework and viability, rejects rational-basis substitution, recognizes appropriately indicated viability examinations as consistent with Roe, and condemns medically useless/risky tests even on ordinary rationality. Reliance includes women's settled life arrangements and equal participation. Recognizes distinction between refusal of subsidy and turning essentially private care into forbidden public care.
- **BA**: Blackmun, Ashcroft separate, 462 U.S. 476, 494–505; June 15, 1983; joined by Stevens. Important health objective and no significant interference govern first-trimester ancillary regulation; unsupported $40 pathology cost matters to poor women; doctors can record reasons without a second doctor being necessary. Rejects the then-present parental/judicial-veto scheme and an invented federal saving construction of unqualified state text.
- **BO**: Blackmun, Ohio v. Akron dissent, 497 U.S. 502, 525–542; June 25, 1990. Treats Bellotti maturity/best-interest alternatives, anonymity and expedition as minimum safeguards; criticizes the concrete pleading, delay, proof and physician-notification burdens, cumulatively and separately. Earlier BA's broader disagreement is not erased; BO supplies a later route for evaluating the actual bypass instead of mechanically rejecting every parental rule.
- **ST**: Stevens, Thornburgh concurrence, 476 U.S. 747, 772–782; June 11, 1986. Childbearing decisions receive heightened protection, not ordinary economic regulation; secular potential-life interests develop during pregnancy; majority disagreement with a woman's choice cannot itself deprive her of liberty. Stare decisis is not absolute, but stability and the enduring contraception/liberty foundations matter. Harlan's historically informed judgment replaces no mechanical formula.
- **SW**: Stevens, Webster separate, 492 U.S. 490, 560–572; July 3, 1989. Viability testing can satisfy Roe if medically indicated; refuses to erase mandatory statutory language through construction; distinguishes medically useful advice from purposeless costs; rejects a theory of life that overrides individual liberty. Government need not be silent, but state-imposed coercion is different from private advice.
- **SH**: Stevens, Hodgson writing, 497 U.S. 417, especially Parts III, V–VIII and notes; June 25, 1990. State carries justification where the law places obstacles in the path of protected choice; interests and actual fit matter before the obstacle becomes an absolute denial. One-parent participation and a genuinely helpful consultation period can be reasonable; a second-parent rule with no useful fit is not cured by forcing a consenting parent and minor through court. Distinguishes adult fixed delay in Akron expressly. General childbearing discussion in Part III was not a majority holding, but is Stevens's own writing.
- **SO**: Stevens, Ohio v. Akron concurrence, 497 U.S. 502, 521–525; June 25, 1990. Joins Parts I–IV, not Part V; sustains facially adequate one-parent notice/bypass without inventing its future maladministration, requires an effective mature/best-interest exception, and permits reasonable steps at physician notice while preserving Akron's different adult counseling rule. Recognizes adjudication may change on an actual administrative record.
- **SR**: Stevens, Riley separate, 487 U.S. 781 (1988), joining Parts I–III and disagreeing only about licensing Part IV. Compelled noncommercial charitable speech cannot be put outside protection by a commercial label; insignificant licensing burden absent evidence of delay is different. This is a joined speech proposition, not an abortion speech holding.
- **SP**: Souter, Payne concurrence joined by Kennedy, 501 U.S. 808; June 27, 1991; full own writing in `prior/payne-souter.txt`. Constitutional error alone does not justify overruling; a special justification is required. Concrete unworkability/internal doctrinal tension can justify partial overruling while other categories remain undecided. The information excluded there was morally relevant, and ordinary due-process protections could police inflammatory presentation; it establishes neither categorical freedom to compel speech nor an abortion test.

Earlier **simulated public** sources, all actually read in `output/`, are mapped with exact quotations and joins in `entering_law.md`: **F** Foucha, May 18 (chunk9; Blackmun/Stevens/Souter join the liberty holding and procedural discussion; all three also join White's noncontrolling equality section); **R** Riggins, May 18 (chunk9; all three join O'Connor's State-justification/less-intrusive-treatment holding); **L** Lee, June 24 (chunk13; Blackmun authors sponsorship holding, all three join both sponsorship and Kennedy pressure grounds; Stevens joins Souter's separate historical-neutrality writing); **M** Medina, June 22 (chunk13; Blackmun/Stevens dissent, Souter joins O'Connor's practical-fairness concurrence sustaining the particular defendant preponderance burden); **C** Collins, February 26 (chunk5; Stevens authors, all three join constitutional-source limits); **H** Hilton, December 16 (chunk3; Stevens/Souter join Kennedy's preserved statutory-coverage precedent; Blackmun writes broader judgment concurrence); **Q** Quill, May 26 (chunk9; Stevens authors, Blackmun/Souter join the due-process holding and Stevens's Commerce plurality); **Mc** McCollum, June 18 (chunk12; Blackmun authors, Stevens/Souter join); **Hu** Hudson, February 25 (chunk5; Stevens and Blackmun narrower writings, Souter joins O'Connor); **W** Wright, June 19 (chunk12; Souter's threshold Teague writing alone). None supplies a previous abortion-specific commitment.

Every row below lists its own-writing key first and its pertinent public-continuity key second. A repeated key incorporates only the specific propositions stated above. It does not treat unrelated criminal procedure or religion law as controlling abortion law.

## Statutory qualifications used by every row

The following terms accompany, and are incorporated into, every provision reference in the matrices; no row relies on an unnamed exception. All are **statutory text** in the supplied statutory source unless a different source is named.

**Emergency/disclosure protection:** §3203 applies to a condition that, on the physician's good-faith clinical judgment, so complicates the woman's medical condition as to necessitate immediate abortion to avert death, or for which delay creates a serious risk of substantial and irreversible impairment of a major bodily function. The **Third Circuit construction**, 947 F.2d 682's emergency discussion, covers significant health threats prospectively including onset of preeclampsia, inevitable abortion and premature ruptured membranes; it does not demand waiting for shock/infection. That is a federal construction, not a Pennsylvania Supreme Court holding. §3205(b) requires explanation of emergency indications before abortion if possible. The distinct §3205(c) affirmative defense requires the physician to prove by a preponderance a reasonable belief that furnishing subsection (a)'s information would have a severely adverse effect on the woman's physical or mental health. It does not itself waive delay. The supplied text has OCR subsection-label irregularities identified in the neutral packet.

**Information/receipt:** §3205(a)(1) medical facts are orally conveyed by the performing or referring physician at least 24 hours before abortion; (a)(2) permits the listed qualified delegate to convey notice of optional free printed material, possible prenatal/birth/neonatal assistance and paternal support. For paternal-support disclosure, **“In the case of rape, this information may be omitted.”** This is permission, without police reporting, and differs from the spousal-assault exception below. Printed material is furnished only if the woman chooses it; neither reading nor accepting it is compulsory. Written certification under (a)(4) establishes receipt of required information, not agreement. Section 3208 requires objective, nonjudgmental scientific content and lists of actual assistance/adoption agencies. District findings 181–189 concern particular directory omissions and misinformation by some listed agencies, with providers able to criticize and supplement; they do not find every state publication false.

**Parent:** §3206(a) requires, except in a medical emergency or as otherwise provided in the section, the informed consent of both the pregnant woman and one parent when she is under18 and not emancipated; for a woman adjudged incompetent it requires her guardian's informed consent. The parent or guardian must consider only the child's or ward's best interests. If the pregnancy results from incest and the father is a party to the incestuous act, the pregnant woman need obtain only her mother's consent. Under §3206(b), **if both parents have died or are otherwise unavailable to the physician within a reasonable time and in a reasonable manner**, the consent of the woman's guardian or guardians is sufficient. If her parents are divorced, consent of the parent having custody is sufficient. **If neither any parent nor a legal guardian is available to the physician within a reasonable time and in a reasonable manner**, consent of any adult person standing in loco parentis is sufficient. The minor may elect bypass without first approaching a parent: maturity/capacity and informed consent, or abortion in her best interests despite immaturity. Statutory safeguards provide counsel, confidentiality/sealed records and prompt disposition (three business days initially, five business days on appeal in the quoted operative safeguards). No current independent bypass-adequacy attack is developed. **No statute expressly commands a clinic visit by the parent:** district finding232 describes clinics' intended compliance/standard-of-care practice; Third Circuit footnote23 reserves construction and reasons bypass would cure even an assumed visit requirement. The incompetent-adult/guardian language is supplied text, without a developed independent challenge.

**Spouse:** §3209 requires a signed nonnotarized certification of notice with a false-statement warning, or an exception certification that the husband is not the father, cannot be located after diligent effort, the pregnancy resulted from spousal sexual assault under §3128 reported to an agency with jurisdiction, or the woman has reason to believe notice likely to result in bodily injury to her by her spouse or another. Medical emergency independently excuses notice. The incorporated assault offense includes force, threatening forcible compulsion that prevents resistance by a person of reasonable resolution, or intercourse with an unconscious person; the **90-day report condition is district finding297's account of incorporated §3128 law**, not a freestanding phrase in §3209. The statute has no general exception for psychological injury, economic retaliation, divorce/custody threats, exposure, or harm to children/others. Likely bodily injury to the woman is not silently expanded to all coercion.

**Reports:** §3214(a)'s individual reports are confidential and omit patient names. **District findings and Third Circuit**, not the face of (a) alone, establish adequate actual safeguards; good-cause judicial authorization governs law-enforcement disclosure, and annual statistics cannot identify physician/facility/patient. The appealed identity issue is referring physician, not performing physician. (a)(8) records basis for necessity under §3211(b)(1) to prevent death/substantial irreversible impairment; (a)(10) explains an emergency excusing statutory compliance; (a)(11) records §3210(a) diagnostic inquiries, examinations/tests, and basis for gestational-age judgment, not merely the resulting age. (a)(12) includes marital status, notice and reasons notice was not given; these are separable inquiries. Unappealed ordinary records remain outside merits reopening.

**Public facility reports:** §3207(b) makes facility affiliation/ownership reports public if state funds were received within 12 calendar months before the request to inspect or copy; otherwise access is confined to law enforcement/licensing officials for official duties. Noncompliance incurs $500 per day. §3214(f) makes quarterly abortion totals by trimester public if state funds were received in the 12 calendar months before filing that report. A no-funds representation receives confidentiality absent contrary evidence. These lookbacks are distinct. Neither provision makes individual patient reports public. The challenged public release is separate from unchallenged agency collection. Act64 §6 permits severance of words, provisions and applications when the remainder can independently operate.

## Blackmun — frozen commitments

Blackmun begins with his actual abortion opinions rather than reconstructing a hypothetical moderate center. His selected general rule remains Roe's protected choice, viability line and trimester-related scrutiny; a more protective minimum may be joined as a minimum without assent to replacing his rule. The present source corrections materially change some applications: true confidentiality, optional printed material, rape permission, a prospective emergency construction and express severability cannot be ignored. BA's broad parental objection is acknowledged, while the actual appealed increment and BO's later case-specific bypass analysis bound this adjudication.

## Stevens — frozen commitments

Stevens's governing proposal protects choice and tests what a regulation actually does and whether its justification fits. SH is unusually direct evidence for a framework capable of invalidating burdens below complete obstruction and placing justification on the State. But his own writings also accept useful one-parent participation, genuine medical advice, sensible facial limits and ordinary reporting. Truthful optional information and the corrected statute require fresh applications; BT's prior disposition is not itself a present vote. He will accept restatement of doctrine that preserves its constitutional protection and reasoned scrutiny without promising every piece of prior trimester machinery is immutable.

## Souter — frozen commitments and bounded uncertainty

Souter has **no date-eligible abortion writing**. No row claims otherwise. His own SP writing and his actual prior-term public joins provide method, while the abortion precedents supply entering law. SP demands special justification, recognizes partial doctrinal correction, and tests the actual defect and retained safeguards; F/R/L show sensitivity to actual coercion and burdens, while M/W/C caution against turning that sensitivity into a universal burden allocation or substantive test. The unresolved question is whether he would personally replace Roe's doctrinal machinery with a comprehensive abortion formula. The bounded conclusion here is **retain the constitutional protection and existing precedents as necessary, decide these provisions on their proved operation, and decline to endorse either a universal substantial-obstacle-only threshold or a new universal two-tier balancing framework before the actual proposed rationale is tested**. This is a frozen refusal to supply a missing abortion philosophy, not an uncast vote on the components below. Any later comprehensive joinder requires an explicit reconciliation explaining why it is compatible with, or changes, this boundary.

## Framework joinder ceiling and assembly handoff

These are **provisional commitments**, not assignments or published opinion topology. Blackmun will join protected choice, viability, health, actual coercion/obstacle prohibition and inadequate-fit invalidations as minimum protections, but refuses replacement of his Roe/trimester scrutiny with a weaker exclusive formula. Stevens will join a concrete framework preserving choice/viability/health, independently prohibiting substantial obstacles to protected care, testing meaningful lesser burdens for permissible justification and fit, and putting that justification on the State once a meaningful burden is shown; he refuses treating the State's wish to discourage the protected choice alone as sufficient justification, ignoring cumulative/affected-woman burdens, or importing a minor-consultation exception into adult delay. Souter joins core preservation and obstacle prohibition as a floor, rejects immunity for every lesser burden, but has no frozen commitment to either a new comprehensive threshold-only or a new comprehensive two-tier rule; exact propositions and any revision require reconciliation rather than an invented preexisting abortion position.

For all three, proof of a serious burden on a relevant class cannot be answered simply by counting women whom the provision does not affect. None adopts an unspecified numerical facial denominator. All require every statutory protection to retain its actual terms, distinguish findings from commands, preserve physician judgment in the supplied risk-based emergency construction, and distinguish public facility reports from confidential individual records. No historical lineup or assignment supplies any row. Comparator review must now confirm each component or record a reasoned departure; only afterward may Stone's actual Section II be opened and an opinion-by-opinion join test performed.

## Pre-global-freeze scope refresh and explicit additional commitments

The neutral packet's appended **Neutral scope addendum — spousal compelled speech and emergency vagueness** was personally source-validated and incorporated before any comparator opening. The omission concerned the scope catalog, not new evidence or a changed substantive conclusion. This refreeze adds separate ground/reach rows and does not silently rewrite the prior rows.

**Parent disposition precision:** All three vote to sustain §3206 against the present facial attack without treating district finding232 as an enacted clinic-visit command. Their reservation concerning an actual compelled visit means that ordinary proceedings/application challenges remain possible; it does **not** require a separate special remand to adjudicate a hypothetical visit command or invalidate the entire informed-parent provision. A disposition that affirmatively holds bypass necessarily cures every needless visit remains outside all three commitments. The ordinary mandate implementing the provision-by-provision judgment is unaffected.

**Refreeze status:** The foregoing is the final provisional handoff before the global comparator gate. No historical comparison or Stone text was used in the added rows or the disposition clarification.

### Final parent-content and alternative-ground precision before global freeze

The parent's informed-consent duty is §3206(a)'s text, but the statute does **not** separately define it or expressly incorporate each §3205 delivery mechanism. The district court's pp.1382–1384 analysis used §3205 to define that content and invalidated §3206 additionally on emergency/content grounds. This is a **lower-court construction**, distinct from the statute and the clinic-attendance finding. The following rows resolve the content question separately; they do not add a clinic-visit command or delete the word informed wholesale.

| Justice; own/public source | Opposed paths and strongest arguments | Exact provisional disposition and joinder |
|---|---|---|
| Blackmun — parental informed content; BT/BA/BO; R | A the ancillary information invalid when compulsorily given to the minor cannot become a mandatory precondition by transmitting it to her parent; B parental deliberation gives the same accurate option information added relevance, even when the woman could decide without it. Strongest B argument is the parent's protective role; strongest A response is that protection concerns the minor's best interests, not State-imposed persuasion, and a consent route cannot reintroduce invalid prerequisites. | Sustain ordinary informed parental consent, including medically relevant nature/risks/alternatives, with elective maturity/best-interest bypass. Invalidate incorporation of the mandatory §3205(a)(2)(i), (ii), and (iii) ancillary commands into the parent's required consent, to the same extent as the commands to the woman. Permit voluntary relevant ancillary counseling, optional materials and accurate certification of lawful receipt. **Affirm the Third Circuit's rejection of facial invalidation of §3206 as a whole, but reverse insofar as its judgment permits enforcement of those invalid incorporated ancillary prerequisites.** No special attendance remand; ordinary mandate implements severance. This is a distinct partial parental-content vote, not an unqualified vote to uphold every informed-parent condition. |
| Stevens — parental informed content; SH/SO/ST; R | A accurate medical and limited financial/material-availability information reasonably supports the parent's best-interest advice; B forcing the same information can burden an already informed parent and child. Strongest B argument is unnecessary repetition; strongest A is the useful parental function, lawful qualified delivery, optional ultimate receipt and lack of an independent prescribed clinic visit. | Sustain the ordinary medical and the narrowly construed accurate ancillary content when used to obtain informed parental consent, with the actual emergency, incest/unavailability and bypass protections. **Affirm the Third Circuit's §3206 facial disposition; no vacatur and no special parental-attendance remand.** Do not imply approval of a mandatory personal clinic appearance, a new nondelegable parental-counseling duty, or a parent-specific waiting period absent an established construction. The woman's invalid fixed24hour and physician-only commands remain invalid regardless of parental participation. |
| Souter — parental informed content; SP; M/R/C | A established informed parental participation can use truthful relevant medical/options information; B §3205's detailed mechanisms should not automatically define every parent's consent or require an unnecessary trip. Strongest B argument is precise text and actual burdens; strongest A is narrow consent information without inventing implementation. | Sustain informed-parent medical and accurate ancillary content at that limited level. **Affirm the Third Circuit's §3206 facial disposition; no vacatur and no special attendance remand.** Reserve an actual enforced visit, special parental wait or personal-delivery construction not established here. The woman's fixed delay and physician monopoly are separately severed. |

**Alternative-ground holding count for each of Blackmun, Stevens and Souter:** No independently sufficient equal-protection holding is selected, either narrow or broad. No independently sufficient general marital-privacy or informational-privacy holding is selected, either narrow or broad. Private decisionmaking, bodily autonomy, absence of a spouse's controlling authority, the actual coercive effects of mandated disclosure, and the relevant woman's ability to exercise protected choice remain parts of the **abortion-liberty rationale**, not a second freestanding constitutional ground. For Stevens, SH's private-family reasoning informs that application; it does not automatically add an independently sufficient holding. All three expressly decline the distinct spousal First Amendment ground and its preservation question as unnecessary after full notice invalidation. Thus none may be counted as silently joining an independent equality, general-privacy or speech holding merely because the disposition or descriptive concerns coincide.

**All three attendance judgments, without alternatives:** No additional remand devoted to statutory attendance construction; no vacatur of §3206 on the supposed presence of an enacted attendance command. All affirm rejection of a facial challenge to §3206 based on that supposed command. They preserve the question only for a properly presented actual construction/application and refuse the universal claim that bypass cures every needless visit. Blackmun's separately specified ancillary-content severance is the sole partial reversal of the parental informed-content disposition in these three rows.

### Actual modeling-clarification log

Before the global freeze and before any comparator or Stone opening, source-catalog review exposed the need for distinct spousal-speech and standalone emergency-vagueness reach rows; the neutral addendum and six rows above were added after checking the actual transcript and provider report. Root's completeness review then requested exact parent judgments and alternative-ground scope. The provisional expressions suggesting a possible attendance remand were normalized to affirmance of the facial attendance ruling without a special remand; Blackmun's invalid ancillary-content incorporation was separately specified, and the absence of independently sufficient equality/general-privacy holdings was made explicit in each original row. A reporter pinpoint range not independently verified for SP was removed; the exact full own writing and case citation remain. These are actual source/clarity refinements during modeling, not invented judicial circulation, historical-comparator departures, or post-Stone movements. The resulting original rows and addenda are the single final provisional position for each component.

# Provisional commitments — White, Scalia, Thomas

**Casey, Nos. 91-744 and 91-902; June 29, 1992.** Mode: single-conversation fallback. Neutral framing was frozen in `neutral-modeling-packet.md` before these commitments were formed. The modeler read that whole packet, the specified full own writings and the public continuity identified below. No Stone supplement, comparator, historical Casey opinions, prior Casey record, or prior Casey commitment was opened. Incidental historical search/IA metadata exposure during source retrieval was previously disclosed; true blindness is unavailable. This is a new issue-specific model, not adoption of a prior commitment. It proposes neither Court-wide result nor authorship.

**Freeze status:** These are the complete provisional commitments supplied for the eight-Justice freeze. A comparator may confirm them or disclose a departure, but cannot supply them. Any post-Stone movement requires an Engine §8 reconciliation audit. A modeler's decisional alternative is not an invented historical vote, dialogue, draft, or concession.

Full own-writing reads: White's Doe/Roe dissent, 410 U.S. 221–223; Danforth concurrence/dissent, 428 U.S. 92–101; Thornburgh dissent, 476 U.S. 786–814; Brennan's Michael M. dissent joined by White, 450 U.S. 488–496; Riley Court opinion joined by White and, except footnote 11, Scalia, 487 U.S. 781–803; Scalia's Riley concurrence, 803–804; Scalia's Webster concurrence, 492 U.S. 532–537; Scalia's Ohio v. Akron Center concurrence, 497 U.S. 520–521. Raw primary files and extraction trace are in `white_scalia_thomas_authority_notes.md`. These writings were read in full, including material notes; selected lines were not treated as substitutes for the whole writing.

Public continuity checked in `output/`: **C5-Collins** (February 26, chunk 5), **C5-Hudson** (February 25, chunk 5), **C9-Foucha** (May 18, chunk 9), **C9-Riggins** (May 18, chunk 9), **C9-Quill** (May 26, chunk 9), **C12-McCollum** (June 18, chunk 12), **C12-Wright** (June 19, chunk 12), **C13-Medina** (June 22, chunk 13), **C13-Lee** (June 24, chunk 13); White's **C3-Hilton** (December 16, chunk 3). Those short citations below identify the exact case/entry, not a generic term-wide tendency. The neutral packet supplies the relevant authors, joins and limits. No Thomas inference rests on Hilton, in which he did not participate. Thomas has no date-eligible abortion writing; his rows explicitly identify the unresolved methodological question and its bounded modeled resolution.

Citation keys: **W-Roe** = White's Doe/Roe dissent; **W-Danforth** = White's Danforth separate writing; **W-Thornburgh** = White's Thornburgh dissent; **W-MichaelM** = his Michael M. dissent join; **Riley-W** = White's full Court-opinion join; **S-Webster**, **S-Ohio**, **S-Riley** = Scalia's own writings just identified, with Riley including his full Court join except footnote 11. Each table row's final field cites both a date-eligible own-writing source and actual simulated public continuity. Thomas's public writings are his available own writings; no abortion authority is falsely attributed to him.

The statutory baseline is the full verbatim statutory appendix and supplemental source quotations in the frozen neutral packet. It is incorporated as the source of each exact provision, not a paraphrase of the prior Supreme Court result. The qualifications stated in the component entries below are statutory unless expressly called findings or constructions. The proposed judgments concern the challenged applications and provisions only, not unappealed items. Sustaining a facially challenged provision does not establish that every future false publication, confidentiality breach or coercive enforcement application is lawful.

### White's spousal-exception precision and conclusion

His sustained facial rule uses §3209's actual text: a signed, nonnotarized notice statement; alternatively a signed, nonnotarized statement that spouse is not father, cannot be located despite diligent effort, pregnancy results from §3128 spousal sexual assault reported to law enforcement with jurisdiction, or she has reason to believe notice likely will cause bodily injury to her by spouse or another. Both statement forms warn false statements are punishable. The medical-emergency exception is §3203's good-faith clinical judgment of immediate abortion to avert death or delay creating serious risk of substantial and irreversible major-function impairment. District finding297 identifies the incorporated assault law's90-day reporting restriction; this is a finding about that law, distinct from the rape permission in §3205(a)(2)(iii). There is no general psychological/economic/child-injury/divorce/custody exception. White does not invent one; his facial conclusion instead disputes the legal consequence of the full found burdens under the sources he accepts. His Danforth position is the primary source; independent equality and privacy objections have been confronted, not absorbed into an abortion label.

## Scalia

Additional own source read fully before these commitments: **S-MichaelH**, Scalia's plurality in Michael H. v. Gerald D.,491U.S.110, including footnote6 and the separate equal-protection/preservation discussion. This supplies Scalia's method and actual limited familial-right reasoning; its result is not an abortion precedent. Footnote6 has only Scalia/Rehnquist and is not attributed to O'Connor or Kennedy. His account expressly distinguishes the fact that liberty extends beyond physical restraint from the particular asserted entitlement's constitutional foundation.

For every row, Path B states the strongest counterargument to Path A. The commitment column states the response to Path B; where a narrower route could avoid choosing, it is named in the next column. Thus neither pathway is presented without an adversarial test.

### Scalia's spousal-exception precision

The §3209 notice and substitute-exception statements are signed and need not be notarized, with false-statement warnings. Substitute certification is available if spouse is not father; diligent effort cannot locate him; pregnancy results from §3128 spousal assault reported to the competent law-enforcement agency; or the woman has reason to believe notice likely will cause bodily injury to her by spouse or another. Section3203's clinical medical emergency independently excuses notice: immediate abortion to avert death or delay creating serious risk of substantial irreversible major-function impairment. District finding297 supplies the incorporated assault law's90-day restriction; neither its reporting requirement nor timing is attached to §3205(a)(2)(iii)'s rape-information permission. Psychological/economic harm, threats to children, divorce/custody retaliation and publicity are not general exceptions. Scalia's rejection of facial invalidity accepts their existence in the record and disputes their legal consequence under his source-specific framework; it does not fabricate statutory protection for them.

## Thomas

**No abortion-writing premise.** Thomas has no date-eligible abortion opinion. His own simulated writings, read from the public record, provide the primary evidence: Hudson and Foucha dissents, Riggins dissent (including his own separate scope objection, which Scalia did not join), McCollum judgment concurrence, Wright principal opinion, and his actual joins in Quill, Medina, Lee and Collins. Those sources establish neither a concealed abortion view nor a preexisting undue-burden formula.

**Baseline versus fresh choice.** Roe and governing progeny enter as precedent; Thomas's failure to have written on abortion does not suspend their force. One supported pathway is exact adherence, reflected in his McCollum application of Edmonson despite disagreement and his Quill retention of the specific Commerce rule. A different pathway, available because the parties squarely present reconsideration here, is to reject the constitutional foundation after comparing text, tradition, institutional limits, workability and reliance. His Quill join also accepts overruling a constitutional due-process rule, demonstrating that adherence is not absolute. The provisional model chooses the second pathway for the Roe foundation, while keeping each independent constitutional claim separate. This is a new modeled conclusion at this event, not a prior position and not a result imported from history.

**Unresolved question and bounded conclusion.** The principal uncertainty is whether Thomas would regard the weight of settled reproductive expectations as sufficient to retain Roe despite his source/history concerns. No own abortion writing resolves it. The bounded conclusion here is that, on the present squarely briefed reconsideration and his source-specific earlier methods, he would decline to recognize elective previability abortion as a fundamental constitutional entitlement and would sustain these regulations under rational review unless a separate constitutional source requires more. He does not deny all substantive liberty, all reliance, all privacy, all sex equality, or all protection for medically necessary care. Component-specific uncertainties below narrow that conclusion; they are not filled by another Justice's or the historical Court's outcome.

For every row Path B supplies the strongest challenge to Path A, and the chosen ground answers Path B at the bounded scope. An unresolved model question is expressly identified rather than represented as a known past Thomas view.

### Thomas's exact spousal qualifications

Section3209 requires a signed, nonnotarized statement of notice, warning that false statements are punishable. A signed, nonnotarized exception statement may instead certify that spouse is not father; cannot be located despite diligent effort; pregnancy results from§3128 spousal assault reported to law enforcement with jurisdiction; or she has reason to believe notice likely will cause bodily injury to her by spouse or another. It too carries the false-statement warning. Medical emergency independently excuses notice under§3203's good-faith clinical judgment: immediate abortion to avert death or delay creating serious risk of substantial irreversible major-function impairment. District finding297 supplies the incorporated assault law's90-day reporting restriction. Section3205(a)(2)(iii)'s rape-information permission has no police-report condition and is not a direction to omit. The statute does not create general exemptions for psychological/economic coercion, threatened harm to children, divorce/custody retaliation or publicity. Thomas's bounded facial sustention accepts that deficiency's factual consequences and asks which independent constitutional source supplies relief; it does not assume a nonexistent exception or equate the absence of formal veto with absence of harm.

## Cross-row assembly controls and final handoff

1. All three Justices' **primary provision judgments** sustain the challenged appealed nonspousal provisions and would reverse the Third Circuit's spousal invalidation. That matching disposition is not a common complete opinion or automatic joinder. Their source, precedent, facial-scope and independent-right grounds differ and require exact formulation testing.
2. None would join affirmative constitutional elective-previability choice, a viability cutoff, a stand-alone substantial-obstacle prohibition, a general lesser-meaningful-burden/deficient-fit rule, or an automatic State justification burden merely on showing meaningful abortion burden. All can join accurate description of the statute, medical/parental procedural safeguards, statement that independent speech/equality/privacy rights remain applicable, and scope/record limits, but only at the precise grounds their rows accept.
3. White's precedent choice is anchored in his own express abortion dissents; Scalia's in his own Webster/Ohio Akron writings and source criticism; Thomas's is a fresh bounded conclusion from general method and actual prior-term public positions, with his McCollum/Quill adherence counterpath unresolved as model uncertainty and explicitly confronted. They are not interchangeable.
4. **Conditional report remedy is not a switched vote.** If another coalition invalidates§3209, each has recognized that its enforcement rationale cannot itself justify the dependent notice/reason fields of§3214(a)(12). Recognition alone does not join invalidation, decide independent marital-status data, or count as a conditional concurrence. Assembly must present the actual severance/remaining-scope formulation, test it against each row, and separately record any conditional remedial join and basis. A changed substantive commitment requires§8 reconciliation, not silent counting.
5. **Guardian and unappealed scope:** no new independent merits ruling on the adult-incompetent guardian class; no reopening district-upheld unappealed ascertainment, most confidential collection or§3214(a)(5)'s gestational-age result. A discrete disclosure/public-release ruling cannot erase all collection.
6. **No broad vagueness holding:** proposed emergency sustention rests on prospective good-faith clinical construction and developed health claim. Record may describe Third Circuit's vagueness ruling and officials' waiver contention without converting them into a fresh independently sufficient Supreme Court vagueness holding.
7. **Adversarial-field convention:** in every row, Path A states its affirmative authority, Path B states the best supported rival and the strongest objection to A, and the selected-ground column explains why that rival does not prevail at the bounded scope. The join-barrier/narrower field records what can be revised without changing the commitment and what would instead require reconciliation. No possible alternative is represented as a past vote.
8. **Framework limits are part of every join test.** A shared 'undue burden' label or matching disposition cannot secure any join to a proposition these rows reject. Conversely, refusal of an abortion framework does not prevent joining an independently justified medical-information, confidentiality, proper-scope or severability proposition. Only actual drafted grounds can answer the later join question.

### Equality standard clarified before freeze

Additional full primary read: **Caban v. Mohammed,441U.S.380**, Powell's whole Court opinion including notes (28,464characters), in `authorities/caban.json`, extracted under `briefs/caban-court-*.txt`. White actually joined this Court opinion. Neither Scalia nor Thomas is attributed a join or an earlier Caban position. Caban states the controlling sex-classification formulation from Craig: an important governmental objective and a substantial relationship between classification and objective; it rejects universal parental-role generalizations and distinguishes actual relationships, preserving unpresented questions rather than deciding them by analogy.

- **White:** applies intermediate scrutiny to the actual husband-entitlement/wife-duty classification, consistent with W-MichaelM and his Caban join. The asserted objective is actual marital/paternal participation in a decision concerning their prospective child, not women's incapacity. He finds the limited notice requirement substantially related to that objective, distinguishing a legal veto and confronting the actual exceptions and abuse findings. The strongest contrary argument is that the compulsory rule burdens the very relationships where participation is coercive, so notice is not a sufficiently tailored protection of legitimate participation. His response is that intermediate scrutiny does not require an individualized relationship-quality adjudication before any factual notice, while the bodily-injury, nonpaternity, location, assault and medical-emergency provisions constrain the duty. This is his source-specific equality conclusion, not a finding that every harmful relationship is exempt or a rational-basis substitution.
- **Scalia:** **assumes without deciding that intermediate scrutiny applies**, rather than claiming pregnancy removes all sex classification. Applying the important-objective/substantial-relationship test, would reject the facial equality claim for the actual limited notice and parental-participation fit described in his row. He accepts that Caban forbids a blanket presumption mothers and fathers have categorically different interests; the present rationale recognizes the father's actual prospective-parent interest without granting control over the procedure. The strongest contrary argument is the unequal legal power and the coercive affected population, not merely different biology. He concludes that notice's information function and the statute's actual limiting conditions are sufficiently related to the important interest, without treating Michael H.'s child-status rationality test as the governing sex test. Whether this classification independently requires that tier is left undecided.
- **Thomas:** likewise **assumes without deciding intermediate scrutiny**, applying existing sex-equality precedent rather than inventing a Thomas abortion/equality writing. The bounded modeled conclusion is that a factual notice duty concerning the spouse's prospective child is substantially related to the important actual participation interest, with no legal veto or ideological assent. The strongest counterargument is that a husband-only right/wife-only duty enforces a relation of authority precisely where consensual dialogue is absent; his answer rests on the distinction between information and legal control plus actual statutory limits, not a claim no injury occurs. Remaining uncertainty is both the classification's proper tier and how his method would resolve a proved coercive application. His assumption supplies an answer at the governing heightened standard without resolving those broader questions.

## Historical facts used, with authority-level limits

O’Connor, Kennedy and Souter jointly authored the historical opinion. The source identifies PartsI,II,III,V-A,V-C,VI as the Court’s opinion; Stevens additionally joined V-E, making that reporting writing four; IV,V-B,V-D were the trio’s writing. Thus a historical judgment majority sustaining a provision is not automatically five signatures for the trio’s rationale. The runtime comparator’s grouped summaries of counseling, parental and reporting votes must be disaggregated against the other historical writings before an all-Justice historical table is published. This review confirms the **individual O’Connor and Kennedy positions**, not every other Justice’s vote on every subitem.

Historical PartI, at846, describes retained protection for previability choice, the inability of State interests to support a prohibition or substantial obstacle before viability, postviability restriction with life/health protection, and legitimate maternal-health/potential-life interests from the outset. PartIV, at872–879, rejects trimester machinery and gives the general purpose-or-effect substantial-obstacle formulation. It expressly acknowledges inconsistent earlier uses, cites O’Connor’s earlier possibility of a justified undue burden, and rejects that possibility for the fetal-life regulation described. Its broad paragraph also addresses a substantial obstacle serving “some other valid state interest”; its summary separately speaks of **unnecessary** health regulation. Those distinctions must be retained. It is inaccurate either to call the whole historical exposition simply O’Connor’s unchanged Akron test or to omit its qualifier concerning unnecessary health regulation.

Historical medical emergency sustention appears at879–880; informed consent, medical/ancillary information, physician delivery and waiting at881–887; spousal notice at887–898; parental consent/bypass at899–900; reports at900–901; the judgment and severability remand at901. Independent counseling First Amendment objections receive a short merits rejection at884 based on factual disclosure within medical practice, with Wooley acknowledged. There is no separate spousal First Amendment holding or freestanding emergency-vagueness holding. Spousal reasoning uses protected liberty, bodily integrity, family privacy and rejection of marital hierarchy; it does **not** separately announce Hogan’s intermediate-scrutiny test as an independently sufficient equal-protection holding.
